Saka missed a large portion of last season due to hamstring, hip and achilles tendon injuries having also been sidelined by another hamstring issue in 2024-25. In total, he has had 11 different injuries since September 2023 and Arteta insisted that he has been trying to ease his workload as a result. “It’s certainly been different in the last year or so,” the Spaniard said when asked if Saka remains robust enough to start every match. “The demands that we are putting on every player are immense. The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower.

“Bukayo against Lille [in the Champions League last week] didn’t start the game because we knew what was happening. We have to play three times in less than six days. And especially when the games are so demanding, until the last minute you are there, you are chasing the game, you want to win. The necessity is to win every game, so we know that. So we are preparing the players for those scenarios and we do the best that we possibly can.”

Saka missed only three Premier League matches in three seasons between 2021 and 2024 and broke the Arsenal club record by playing in 83 consecutive top-flight games. He is already approaching 300 appearances for the club he joined as a seven-year-old and was rewarded with a lucrative new contract in February that made him one of the highest-paid players in the club’s history.

Asked whether he feared Saka could suffer from burnout having made his Arsenal debut three months after his 17th birthday, Arteta said: “I don’t have that feeling at all but something we have to be very mindful of is to create the right ecosystem around the player to fulfil his qualities. We really need to understand, whenever he comes back, how we are going to manage his load, what he is capable of to sustain having an impact in the team.”

Saka had only three weeks off after the World Cup but Arteta rejected suggestions that he should have been given more We want to pick on something, we will find it, but we won’t know whether it is for that or not. Maybe we needed to load those tendons more during those three weeks? Because if you don’t load the tendons, it becomes a problem. Who knows? I don’t know.”

Saka’s absence could hand an opportunity to Max Dowman on Saturday. The 16-year-old has played only nine minutes in the league this season and Arteta feels sure he is ready to make an impact after he became the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history, against David Moyes’s side in March.

“There is something inevitable to go back to that memory and the feeling of the moment. That’s with us, that’s going to stay in that stadium for a long, long time,” said Arteta. “He’s training and every time he’s got a moment to play, he’s showing that he’s a player that is going to impact the game. For sure he’s going to have minutes.”

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing at Bayern training
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany has been ⁠taken ⁠to ​hospital after the Bayern Munich coach felt unwell during training ⁠on Friday.

The Belgian, ​who ‌had been ‌nursing a virus in ‌recent days, was coaching his team before feeling unwell and being taken to ‌hospital.

The Bundesliga leaders, who drew 2-2 ​at home against Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, are due ​to ​travel to ​Freiburg on Sunday. Kompany was on the bench for the Arsenal game despite the viral infection.

Bayern said on their website: “Vincent Kompany required medical ⁠attention after collapsing during a training session for ​Bayern’s reserve team. The ‌head coach of the professional squad had been observing ‌the second team’s session.

“Kompany is currently undergoing a thorough examination in the hospital and will remain under medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage all training ‌and match-related operations.“

Max Eberl, Bayern’s sporting director, said: “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority. At Bayern, we will do everything ​we ​can to ensure he ​makes a speedy recovery.

“Vinnie is receiving ​all the ‌necessary medical care ​and ​support, and he will be given as much time as he needs. Everyone at FC Bayern wishes Vinnie a quick recovery.”

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
Sports.content:
Are the team underperforming?

Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA

There have been so many arrivals and departures on Tyneside in recent months that it’s too early to say. Any team that sold their three best players – Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimarães in Newcastle’s case – during the summer would expect a degree of disruption. Eight signings were made, with four aged 20 and under and the others aged 24 and under, and only one (Nico González) had Premier League experience. Throw in a change of manager and an almost entirely new backroom staff and playing style three weeks before the season and teething troubles seem almost inevitable. LT

How much pressure is the manager under?

Sage is sailing extremely close to the wind and was warned after the Brighton game that things must improve quickly or he will be shown the door. It is understood that the Palace chair, Steve Parish, has yet to be convinced by the manager who led Lens to the French Cup last season and has demanded improvements in defence. After the creditable Europa League draw with Besiktas in midweek, Sunday’s meeting with Newcastle is crucial to his future. Thomas Frank and Kieran McKenna are likely candidates should Sage get sacked. Ipswich would be due substantial compensation for McKenna despite him leaving Portman Road in the summer, which could be a major hurdle. EA

View image in fullscreen Adam Wharton (centre) looks dejected during Crystal Palace’s defeat at Brighton. Photograph: Robbie Hoad/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

Very little internally but, externally, the honeymoon is over. Newcastle paid Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli £9.5m compensation for Matthias Jaissle, convinced that the 38-year-old German and his “vertical football” were ideal fits. David Hopkinson, the chief executive, and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, are very impressed by Jaissle’s management style, particularly his collaborative approach. They appreciate that Eddie Howe’s successor is new to the Premier League, did not have a proper pre-season and is coping with a raft of injuries. All parties remain sufficiently realistic to predict a season of “ups and downs” but Newcastle’s Saudi Arabian owners crave a return to Europe. Many fans believe Jaissle’s football is old-school, rudimentary long ball with a fancy name, and believe his system and team selections have been flawed. They fear he may be a slave to philosophy. LT

How much responsibility does the manager bear?

Palace have looked a shadow of the side that won three trophies in the space of 12 months under Glasner and Sage must take some of the blame. He fell out with Parish after failing to sign several of his preferred targets in the summer, but it was his decision to break up the Adam Wharton-Daichi Kamada axis in central midfield having brought in Quinten Timber on deadline day. While the Dutchman, who missed the game in Turkey due to injury, has provided extra energy and Kamada has excelled in a more advanced role, Wharton has been struggling defensively. Palace looked much more solid when Wharton and Kamada started together against Besiktas – surely Sage will now stick with the partnership that served Glasner so well. EA

Jaissle’s belief in a gung-ho 4-2-3-1 featuring a classic No 10 is serving him badly at Newcastle, where he does not possess a natural attacking playmaker. It is also leaving González, a holding midfielder, frequently overrun and in need of additional support. With Malick Thiaw and, particularly, Sven Botman struggling in central defence, a switch to a more stable 3-5-2 may be sensible. More importantly, changing the philosophy to a more contain-and-counterattack approach would help camouflage the flaws and make the most of the team’s blistering attacking pace. Jaissle’s high-pressing, attack-minded tactics often appear overly high-risk. His critics fear he may prove to be another Ruben Amorim but Newcastle insiders insist Howe’s successor will prove more flexible than he may seem. Newcastle have not kept a league clean sheet for 13 games, equalling a club record, but six of those came under Howe. LT

How much is beyond the manager’s control?

A typically chaotic end to the transfer window left Sage with a bloated squad but insufficient leadership at the back after selling Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea. Axel Disasi’s three-match ban due to a reckless red card against Ipswich, after he arrived on loan from Stamford Bridge along with the promising Italian teenager Honest Ahanor, hasn’t helped. Parish and the sporting director, Matt Hobbs, deserve criticism for not bringing in more experienced replacements, with the latter’s position also thought to be under heavy scrutiny. Sage has also had to deal with unhappy attackers in Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, who made no secret of their desire to leave Selhurst Park in the summer. EA

Quite a lot. Given his late arrival, Jaissle had limited influence over Wilson’s eight summer signings. He has, though, apparently swiftly decided that Aladji Bamba (£34m from Monaco) and Bazoumana Touré (£43m from Hoffenheim) are not ready to be thrown into Premier League combat. Similarly, the fleet-footed £51m former Lille forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo looks as if he is going to need time to adjust. Newcastle’s policy of generally recruiting players under 25 dictates the dressing room is a little light on leadership. Meanwhile iIt is hard to say whether the manager’s high-intensity training bears any responsibility for a lengthy injury list, with Anthony Elanga, Tino Livramento and Jacob Ramsey notable absentees. LT

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Matias Fernandez-Pardo, seen here rounding Coventry keeper Carl Rushworth but failing to score, will need time to adjust to the Premier League. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

How important is winning this game?

After seeing positive signs against Besiktas, as Mateta scored on his first start since the opening day, three points on Sunday will be crucial for Sage. Yet while Palace haven’t lost to Newcastle at home since November 2020, Jaissle’s side have had extra time to prepare and will present a difficult challenge. EA

Given that Newcastle are 11th it is far from imperative. And yet after a demoralising 4-1 defeat at Coventry and a 1-0 home reverse against Aston Villa, victory would offer much-needed reassurance regarding the team’s potential and boost player confidence, not to mention quieten the social-media noise surrounding Jaissle and his tactics. LT

Are there any reasons for optimism?

Palace’s summer net spend of almost £40m in profit was the second lowest in the Premier League behind Aston Villa. They also have American owners who are estimated to be worth a combined £10bn. But Parish revealed last month that he is still looking for extra funding for the new main stand at Selhurst Park, with Woody Johnson, Josh Harris and David Blitzer thought to be open to selling their shares after Palace enlisted Raine Group to seek fresh investment in the club. So there is plenty riding on making sure there is no prospect of being relegated. Sage showed at Lens that he is capable of building a winning team and needs time to do that. EA

Yes, quite a few. Jaissle, understandably, does not want to overplay the 18-year-old central midfielder Sean Steur but the summer signing from Ajax is a joy to watch, has a wonderful passing range and looks capable of reaching the top. Lewis Hall, the England left-back, looks to be going from strength to strength and is capable of elevating standards. Despite an undoubted dogmatic streak, Jaissle appears intelligent – and humble – enough to learn from his mistakes and make necessary adjustments. Club insiders cite his refreshing willingness to listen. Newcastle also possess several extremely quick attacking players – and, as coaches rarely tire of pointing out: “If you’ve got pace, you’ve got a chance.” LT

Sports.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
Sports.content:
Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024, the midfielder entered – and won – a running race.

Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor.

Gross was moving from Brighton to Borussia Dortmund after seven years in the Premier League and reported to his boyhood club for pre-season training days later. Running is an obsession for Gross, as it is for his former teammate James Milner, who revealed last month he was training for a marathon after finally hanging up his boots, and that has shown since he returned for a second spell at the Amex in January for a bargain £1.2m.

“I think he’s looking in his free time now: ‘Where can I run a race?’ Because he will never stand still,” joked Brighton’s head coach, Fabian Hürzeler, after the 35-year-old scored the opening goal in a 3-0 victory over Arsenal last month. “ During the off-season he’s never the person who can lay on the beach for several hours and do nothing. He always needs to do something.”

Given that Gross has this season racked up an average distance of more than 11.5km per match and has covered the third-most ground of any player in the Premier League, it is no surprise Hürzeler has compared his compatriot to a good wine: “The older the wine gets, the better it gets.”

That analysis is borne out by the rest of his statistics this season as Brighton have emerged as challengers for Champions League qualification, at the very least, before Sunday’s game at Liverpool. Not only has Gross, the Premier League’s player of the month for September, contributed a combined seven goals and assists, he is in the top five for several other metrics such as big chances created (six), chances created from open play (14) and line-breaking passes leading to a goal (three). In a team that have scored the fourth-most goals (23) in Premier League history after seven games, Gross has been the standout performer.

View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross (in white) up against Jablonec's Matej Polidar in the Conference League. The match finished 0-0. Photograph: David W Cerny/Reuters

“Sometimes he’s just one step ahead than his opponent,” said Hürzeler, who is understood to have been instrumental in bringing back Gross. “He might not be the quickest player, but he can be the quickest in the head and sometimes being the quickest in the head is very helpful. No one expected that it would be this good. But it also shows that he still has this capacity in his body.”

At a club where experience is valued despite Hürzeler being the youngest permanent manager in the Premier League’s history, insiders describe Gross as the perfect role model for some of Brighton’s younger players. Charalampos Kostoulas has scored three goals in his past four league matches and the 19-year-old Greece striker is clearly thriving alongside the man who is approaching 300 appearances for the club. Diego Gómez, the dynamic Paraguayan who scored a goal-of-the-season contender against Crystal Palace that will go down in Brighton folklore, the homegrown talent Jack Hinshelwood and the midfield linchpin Yasin Ayari are others benefiting from his vast experience, as is Hürzeler.

Gross managed 75 Brighton goals and assists after joining from Ingolstadt in 2017 in the summer when Brighton were promoted. His departure for Dortmund, a year after his first Germany cap, was to fulfil a boyhood dream but there was always something drawing Gross – who wears a long-sleeve shirt owing to a grass allergy – back to the club where he is known as the Kaiser.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It was really difficult,” Gross said of his Brighton exit. “Only something really special got me out of here. There were a couple of other options [before returning], but Brighton was always the priority. I just stayed in touch with all the lads over the time away. Maybe you watch less of the games or you don’t stay in touch as much any more, it gets less and less. But it never really did.”

Gross retiring from international football after the World Cup has also been to Brighton’s benefit. His status as a club legend was augmented by delivering the free-kick that Palace’s Jaydee Canvot headed into his own net during the 5-0 humiliation on Sunday. That was the third game in a row in which Gross has provided an assist and he has an opportunity to become the oldest player to make it four since Chelsea’s Gianfranco Zola in December 2002.

The trip to Anfield continues a gruelling run of five away fixtures in a row. Brighton drew at the Czech club Jablonec on Thursday in the Conference League and after Sunday they go to Manchester City twice in four days – the first in the Carabao Cup – before heading to Spain to play Getafe. It will test Brighton’s mettle after their spectacular start. Hürzeler can count on Gross – who has started every game in all competitions – to last the course.

Sports.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
Sports.content:
It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches but all eyes are on Renée Slegers.

Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day.

The Arsenal hierarchy are understood to remain behind Slegers, but for how long? The answer may hinge on Saturday lunchtime’s result. However much goodwill the Dutchwoman gained for guiding Arsenal to Champions League glory in May 2025, the simple truth is, it is unacceptable for a club with one of the biggest budgets in the world to be 12 points behind the leaders after six games.

That gap is why the draw with Birmingham not only pretty much extinguished Arsenal’s title hopes but also burned a hole in their secondary domestic objective – Champions League qualification. The unthinkable prospect of failure appears a genuine possibility: they are nine points adrift of third-placed London City. Arsenal need a derby win on Saturday but also a winning run to reverse the slide, and there is little evidence to suggest such a turnaround is close.

Arsenal have the worst shot conversion rate in the league (4.1%) and, according to Stats Perform, the third-worst shooting accuracy (30.6%) and third-lowest average xG per shot (0.09) despite averaging over 60% possession. Slegers’s persistence in deploying Alessia Russo – widely regarded as one of Europe’s best No 9s – in the No 10 role has baffled supporters and commentators alike. Russo has scored more WSL goals against Tottenham (eight) than any other player so Saturday’s game may be the perfect moment for that to change.

View image in fullscreen Arsenal’s Alessia Russo and Caitlin Foord wheel away after a goal against Tottenham in February 2025 – however, Russo has not flourished as a No 10 this season. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Arsenal have struggled against low blocks for a number of seasons, though, so not all fault lies at Slegers’s door. Nonetheless, the 37-year-old was substantially backed in the summer, with Arsenal enjoying perhaps their strongest transfer window in recent memory. So far though they have looked confounded tactically, bruised mentally and lacking the self-belief to grab a game by the scruff of its neck.

Asked if she was surprised to still be in her job, Slegers said: “That’s not something I think about. It’s about, ‘where are we as a group?’ and ‘what are we working towards?’ It’s absolutely not what we expected [our recent results] or what we wanted. But I’m in the here and now, and we are preparing for the north London derby. We have the group together. Everyone is going in the same direction and the fuel and motivation is sky high, because of the fans that will be there for us. That’s where my focus will be.”

Asked how imperative it is that Arsenal climb back up into a Champions League place this season, Slegers added: “Of course that’s in the back of our heads, but what we need right now is to get back to winning ways. We can only do that with the next game in front of us so that’s why the next game in front of us is the most important right now.”

Slegers has maintained after last weekend’s draw that Arsenal will recover when they fix some “details and margins”. Perhaps taking on a Tottenham side who have become only the second team in history to concede six or more goals in consecutive WSL games is the perfect opportunity.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It is a little bit of game intelligence and smartness in moments,” said the Spurs head coach, Martin Ho, insisting he is not worried about his team’s defending in the long-term. “There have been certain aspects that, collectively, players and staff, we were not happy with in certain moments, and we have to make sure we correct them. At the moment we’re getting heavily punished for some small errors with the ball that we’re making.”

The Englishman also only had praise for Arsenal’s qualities when speaking on Friday morning. “If you try and underestimate a team with Arsenal’s quality you’re in for trouble,” he said. Asked about Arsenal’s poor run, Ho added: “Arsenal aren’t a bad side. Their possession stats are probably the highest in the league, alongside Manchester City. Their goalscoring chances and touches in the opposition box are very, very high. They have world-class players.”

Last season’s runners-up do have world-class players but it is high time for them to play like a cohesive team.

Sports.title: Premier League release statement as Issa Diop told he’s lucky to avoid red card
Sports.content:
Issa Diop was 'so, so lucky' to avoid being shown a red card after bringing James McAtee down as he raced through on goal.

The Ipswich defender was only given a yellow card for the poor challenge, which clattered the Nottingham Forest attacker.

3 Diop was only shown a yellow card after wiping out McAtee as he raced through on goal at Portman Road Credit: Getty

McAtee touched the ball past Diop and looked to be clean through on goal, but as he seemingly broke free, his opponent slid across his path, taking him out.

At first, referee Thomas Bramall didn't even award a free-kick, despite the Moroccan international getting nowhere near the ball.

However, after the ball went out of play, the official paused the match as VAR took a look at the incident.

Bramall was then called over the VAR monitor, and he watched multiple replays of the tackle from Diop on McAtee.

Nottingham Forest manager Oliver Glasner was incensed on the touchline after seeing Diop originally avoid punishment.

And he was then left baffled again, as Bramall only opted to give the Ipswich centre-back a yellow card instead of red, pointing out that McAtee's touch was going away from goal.

Diop 'very lucky' to avoid red

On talkSPORT's commentary from Portman Road, Joe Shennan explained: "Diop is booked, it is a free-kick to Forest, but the referee rules that there is a covering defender."

Dean Ashton then added: "I think he was saying it was the touch that took it away from goal, and I'm not so sure about it...

"He's very lucky, Diop, a ludicrous decision to make that challenge when there's no way McAtee has got the pace to outrun him.

"Just unbelievable to make that decision and so, so lucky for that to only be a yellow card."

3 After watching a few replays of the incident on the VAR monitor, Bramall decided to only give Diop a yellow Credit: Getty

Premier League explanation

After the incident, the Premier League confirmed the reasoning behind the decision to only book Diop.

In a post on their Match Centre account on X, they wrote: "After VAR review for a possible denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity (DOGSO), the referee issued a yellow card to Diop for stopping a promising attack."

That came after Bramall said to VAR: “It's a heavy touch, with the defender inside and he knocks the ball away from the goal – I’m going to go direct free-kick and yellow card."

He then announced in the stadium: “After review, there is a foul by Ipswich No.6. However, because the player knocks it to the right side of the goal, the final decision is direct free-kick and a yellow card to No.6”.

Was it the right decision to book Diop?

Diop thinks it was correct for him to not be sent off for his challenge on McAtee, revealing his thoughts post-match.

He told Sky Sports: "I don't think it's a red. I went to tackle because I saw Leif Davis covering. He puts the ball wide and Leif was there to cover.

3 Fortunately for Diop, he had Davis with him and McAtee's touch was going away from goal, so he avoided a red card Credit: Getty

"I don't think it's a red. I was quite confident about that."

Meanwhile, Ashton admitted that Diop was lucky to not be sent off, but shared the same stance as the defender overall.

He said on talkSPORT: "Davis was pretty much next to McAtee; he would have been right there with him, so to me it's not a denial of a goalscoring opportunity as he's right there.

"If he was behind, fair enough, but he's almost on his shoulder.

"If you're sending someone off, it has to be absolutely clear that it's a goalscoring opportunity and it wasn't.

"Davis was there, and the touch was away from goal."

Sports.title: Man United told £100m-rated transfer target would have prevented Como humiliation
Sports.content:
If Declan Rice were in the Manchester United midfield against Como on Wednesday night, they wouldn't have been embarrassed.

That's the opinion of talkSPORT's Rory Jennings, who referenced Erik ten Hag's recent admission that he pushed to sign Rice.



3 Jennings thinks if United had Rice in their midfield against Como, they would have avoided humiliation in the Champions League Credit: Getty

Ten Hag wanted to bring in the eventual £105m Arsenal midfielder during his tenure, but West Ham rejected the move.

Of course, he is now one of the best midfielders in the Premier League and Europe, starring for the Gunners and England.

Rice didn't end up at Man United, who have gone on to bring in Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in this year's summer window.



The new pair started in Italy against Como, with fellow arrival Carlos Baleba coming off the bench to get some minutes too.

Captain Bruno Fernandes, who shockingly took aim at Michael Carrick's tactics post-match, also took up part of the midfield.



The Red Devils went on to be humiliated by Cesc Fabregas' side, but Jennings thinks that if Rice had been signed under Ten Hag, he would have made the difference on Wednesday evening.

'It's really that simple'

Speaking on the latest episode of talkSPORT BET's Studs Up, he said: "If Bruno Fernandes didn't play for Man United and Declan Rice did, which is what Ten Hag said...



"If Rice was playing for Man United, you don't lose 4-1 in Como. It's really that simple."

Mentioning Ten Hag's admission of wanting to sign Harry Kane too, Jennings added: "The fact that you didn't get him over the line, that was John Murtough's time, wasn't it? Ridiculous.

"Imagine that team but with Declan Rice and Harry Kane...which was what Ten Hag wanted.

3 Ex-United manager Ten Hag admitted that he tried to sign Rice when he was in charge Credit: Getty



3 The Red Devils were thrashed 4-1 by Como to make it seven games without a win in all competitions - could Rice have made a difference? Credit: Getty

"I'm not saying Ten Hag deserves massive credit for wanting Kane. You don't get credit for wanting the best players.

"Whoever the manager of Man United is has been let down by the recruitment, but it doesn't excuse what happened in Como.

"If you do a combined XI of Man United and Como, apart from Nico Paz, the vast majority would be United players."



Jennings shares the thoughts of Lisandro Martinez, who called out the Man United board in a bombshell interview last week.

Martinez stated that the club needed to 'bring more players' this summer, targeting technical director Jason Wilcox.

The Red Devils have started the season miserably, going seven games without a win in all competitions, leading to manager Carrick coming under huge pressure heading into the weekend.

Sports.title: Alan Pardew left hurt by EFL sacking as chairman branded ‘clown of the week’
Sports.content:
Alan Pardew has labelled Bromley chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves a clown after the club sacked manager Andy Woodman.

Woodman was dismissed on Thursday morning after five-and-a-half years in charge following a poor start to the season.

2 Bromley boss Woodman was sacked after just 10 games this season despite achieving two promotions in the last three seasons Credit: Getty

The 55-year-old was the third-longest serving manager in the EFL and Premier League, thriving in his job until this term.

He led Bromley from non-league football to League One for the first time in their history with two promotions in three years, as well as winning the FA Trophy in 2022.

A step up to the third tier has proved tough for the Ravens, though, as they have lost their last four and sit 23rd in the table.

That has spelt the end for Woodman, but ex-Crystal Palace and Newcastle boss Pardew thinks his sacking was very harsh.

Asked whether he was disappointed to see the Bromley boss let go, he told talkSPORT Breakfast: "Yeah, I am.

"I'm glad you brought it up actually because on my show, The Final Word, he will be our Clown of the Week, that chairman, Robin Stanton-Gleaves.

"Ridiculous. They're a non-league team, and Andy Woodman has taken them not just to an FA Trophy final, which they won by the way, they've never done it before.

"He takes them through the National League and then into the Football League; he takes them on a National League budget through League Two. They get to League One, they're still on a League Two budget, really.

"And after ten games, he dispenses with his services as if to say, 'Well, it was all about me and nothing to do with Andy Woodman'.

"It's ridiculous, and I think that it's probably the injustice you see sometimes in the game. That hurts, and that hurt me yesterday."

2 talkSPORT host and ex-manager Pardew is furious with Bromley's owner, Stanton-Gleaves, after he decided to get rid of Woodman as boss Credit: Getty

What has Woodman said on his sacking?

Following his exit from Bromley, Woodman released a statement on Friday via the League Managers Association.

He admitted that he was very disappointed not to be given more time to help the club survive in League One.

"It is with great disappointment that my time at Bromley Football Club has come to an end after five and a half years of continued success and achievement," his statement began.

"When I arrived at the club, we had a vision of where we wanted to take Bromley Football Club. To have taken this club from non-league football to League One in just five seasons, as well as winning the FA Trophy at Wembley against a fantastic Wrexham side, is something I will always be incredibly proud of. These are achievements and moments that will stay with me forever.

"Naturally, I am disappointed that I have not been given the time and opportunity to steer the club through its current difficulties and turn our season around, particularly when we are just one point away from safety. I firmly believe that, given the opportunity and the return of key players from injury, we could have given ourselves every chance of achieving our objective.

After thanking the fans, players and people of Bromley, he added: "I leave knowing that I have given this football club everything I possibly could. I have always approached my role with pride, passion, honesty and an unwavering desire to see Bromley succeed. Taking the club on this journey has been one of the proudest achievements of my managerial career.

"I wish Bromley Football Club every success in the future and sincerely hope that whoever comes in next will treat this club with the same respect, desire, commitment and ambition that I have always tried to demonstrate."

Sports.title: Ronaldinho to play first match in 11 years at age 46 for Serie C side
Sports.content:
Ronaldinho to play first match in 11 years at age 46 for Serie C side

Brazil legend Ronaldinho has been confirmed to play his first professional match in over a decade for Italian Serie C side Ravenna.

The World Cup and Ballon d'Or winner will don his boots again, aged 46, in his team's derby against Forlì on November 15.



4 Ronaldinho's 'R10' brand also supplies its shirts Credit: AFP

Ronaldinho, who is a minority owner at Stadio Bruno Benelli, was announced to have signed with the club as a player this summer.

Ravenna have now confirmed the move wasn't a publicity stunt, as the Barcelona icon will indeed return to the pitch next month.

"[It is] an event set to turn the world's gaze toward the Stadio Bruno Benelli," Ravenna said in a statement.



"The whole soccer world thought it too good to be true, instead we can now officially confirm a grand return: The return of the magic, the smile, and a talent that has captivated generations of fans, regardless of their team loyalties or soccer allegiances."

When did Ronaldinho retire?

The 97-cap Brazilian international officially hung up his boots in 2018 after a brief spell with Fluminense in 2015.



Widely regarded as one of the greatest players ever, Ronaldinho enjoyed a star-studded career for both club and country.

He was a key part of Brazil's 2002 World Cup success, having scored 33 goals across a near century of caps between 1997 and 2013.



Ronaldinho is best remembered for his stint at Barcelona, in which he claimed two LaLiga titles and the Champions League title in 2006.

He was awarded the Ballon d'Or in 2005, and was also named FIFA World Player of the Year twice (back-to-back in 2004 and 2005).

Ronaldinho is one of only 11 players to win the Ballon d'Or, Champions League and World Cup, with Rodri the latest to join the list in July.

4 In his prime, Ronaldinho was one of the best players in world football Credit: Getty



Who are his Italian club Ravenna?

Ronaldinho is already part of the club's ownership group fronted by Ignazio Cipriani, of the Cipriani restaurant brand, having previously come on board to help with Ravenna's marketing.

"From the announcement in Miami … To the warm welcome from fans on the beach in Marina di Ravenna, the anticipation has grown, fueled by a mix of excitement, curiosity, and disbelief," Ravenna said.

"The vision of President Cipriani, which ignited the fans' imaginations and sparked debate well beyond Italy's borders, now has a concrete date.

"Ronaldinho will play at the Benelli, opening a new chapter in a story that never ceases to surprise."



Ravenna currently sit second in Group B of Serie C, the regionalised third tier of Italian football, and are pushing for promotion.

4 Ronaldinho starred alongside Ronaldo Nazario as Brazil lifted the World Cup in 2002 Credit: AFP

The Giallorossi, who are managed by former Inter Milan defender Andrea Mandorlini, have rebuilt themselves up the leagues from amateur level following bankruptcy in 2012.

Ravenna are eight points adrift of Serie C leaders Spezia after 10 games, with only the table toppers earning automatic promotion.



Ronaldinho's debut will mark his second spell in Italy, having previously enjoyed a three-year spell at AC Milan from 2008-11.

"There are footballers who are remembered for what they have won and others also for how they made people feel," Ravenna added.

4 Ronaldinho was presented to fans in a ceremony in August but is yet to make his debut Credit: Getty

"Ronaldinho belongs to that rare breed of champions capable of turning soccer into pure joy -- through an unexpected move, a moment of creative brilliance, a smile that has bridged stadiums and generations alike."



"The wait is almost over. The magic is coming back to the field."

Sports.title: Former Arsenal chief Edu takes up shock new role at League Two club
Sports.content:
Former Arsenal chief Edu takes up shock new role at League Two club

Former Arsenal and Nottingham Forest chief Edu has been handed a surprise new role at League Two side Northampton Town.

The Brazilian will work as a senior advisor to the Cobblers, who have just been taken over by a consortium that includes Alexandre Pato.

2 Edu, a former Arsenal and Nottingham Forest chief, is going to be advising Northampton in a surprise new role Credit: Getty

Edu left his position as Arsenal's sporting director in 2024 and eventually became Global Head of Football at Nottingham Forest.

However, just over a year after joining Forest, he officially left the club in September after months of negotiating an exit.

Things didn't go well for Edu at the City Ground as he was told to stay away from the stadium and training ground by owner Evangelos Marinakis in March amid disappointment in his performance.

Since his departure, he has been named as a member of the board of directors for Bulgarian champions Levski Sofia.

But that's not all he's going to be doing, having been revealed to also be helping out Northampton in a new role.

What is Edu's new role?

Northampton's co-chairman Joao Xavier confirmed that Edu is working with the club during an open forum on Thursday.

He said: “We are very proud to have Alex [Pato] with us and Edu with us too.

“We became friends as he had a role at Nottingham Forest, and I asked him to help me learn more about English football.

“Edu is a senior advisor for one of our partners, acting as an advisor for Levski Sofia and also here, helping us navigate the sporting questions here at the club.

"Not day-to-day, just when we ask him and when we need him.”

2 Edu is going to be working with new Cobblers owners, Sports Alpha Capital, who have Pato as a board member and investor Credit: Getty

A new era in Northampton

Northampton will hope that the help of Edu will see them rise up the League Two table after a slow start to the season.

The Cobblers have only won two of their opening 10 games this term, currently sitting 23rd in the fourth tier.

But this weekend brings their first home game on a Saturday since they were taken over by ex-AC Milan and Chelsea star Pato.

And the club are making it a big occasion, even selling Northampton X Brazil merchandise ahead of the match.

Colchester United are the visitors to Sixfields at 12:30pm.

A win could see them jump out of the relegation zone and build on the positivity created by Edu's appointment and Pato's arrival.

Sports.title: PSG vs Lyon postponed amid police fear with new date to clash with major sporting event
Sports.content:
PSG vs Lyon postponed amid police fear with new date to clash with major sporting event

Paris Saint-Germain’s Ligue 1 clash with Lyon on Sunday has been postponed due to riots in the French capital.

The European champions were scheduled to host their rivals at the Parc des Princes on Sunday evening at 7.45pm local time (8.45pm UK time).



4 The Parc des Princes will now host PSG vs Lyon a day later than expected Credit: AFP

However, the game has now been pushed back after police raised security concerns as Paris prepares for ‌another weekend of protests.

PSG's home ground is located in southwest Paris, a region which has been heavily impacted by the demonstrations.

As a result, the fixture will now take place on Monday evening instead, and will kick off 15 minutes earlier at 8.30pm.



There is plenty riding on the top-of-the-table clash, with Lyon leading the way in Ligue 1 ahead of second-place PSG on goal difference.

Ligue 1 statement

The Ligue de Football Professionnel (LFP), the organisers of Ligue 1, confirmed the rescheduling on Friday following the advice of police.



A statement read: “The LFP acknowledges the order from the Police Prefecture prohibiting the organization of the Paris Saint-Germain — Olympique Lyonnais match, counting towards the 8th day of Ligue 1 McDonald’s, on Sunday 25 October at 8:45 pm and decides, in agreement with Ligue 1+, to postpone the match to Monday 26 October at 8:30 pm.

"The match will be broadcast live on Ligue 1+.”

Ballon d'Or impacted

The decision to reschedule the game and play it a day later means it will now clash with the Ballon d’Or ceremony.



4 Ousmane Dembele could make it back-to-back Ballon d'Or wins on Monday Credit: Getty

The star-studded annual event is being held at the London Palladium Theatre, with England captain Harry Kane among the leading candidates to win.

A number of PSG players are also nominated for the top individual prize, which is currently held by talisman Ousmane Dembele.

Also among the nominees from the back-to-back European champions are Achraf Hakimi, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos.



What is happening in France?

France has been affected for weeks by a nationwide movement in which students have been protesting over a lack of resources in schools.

After largely peaceful protests, the demonstrations intensified on Saturday as they combined with a protest against rising living costs.

4 PSG now have an extra day to prepare for the Lyon clash after beating Barcelona in the Champions League on Wednesday Credit: Getty

This saw events turn violent, with buildings being burned and shops looted as tens of thousands of people hit the streets, leaving the government surprised.



Over 2,400 people were reportedly arrested after scenes of carnage across the country, including in Paris.

In response, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu implemented localised curfews in various cities - including parts of the capital.

Movement of people in sections of Paris was banned from 23:00 local time (22:00 BST) on Monday until 06:00 (05:00 BST) on Tuesday.

4 Police in Paris have struggled to deal with increasingly violent protests Credit: Getty



The unsavoury scenes led to concerns that PSG's midweek clash with Barcelona in the Champions League would be affected.

However, the game went ahead as planned, with Luis Enrique's side claiming an impressive 4-2 win against the Spanish champions.

Sports.title: Brandon Williams joins EFL club after proving his fitness to ex-England manager
Sports.content:
Brandon Williams has sealed his return to professional football by joining Rotherham United on a short-term deal.

The former Manchester United defender, who has not played since August 2025, trained with the Millers earlier this summer.



2 Williams played just 15 minutes in his brief spell with Hull Credit: Getty

The 26-year-old linked up with the League Two side in June, but two months later it was announced that he wouldn't be offered a deal.

However, Rotherham have now confirmed he has penned a short-term contract after proving his fitness to ex-England manager Steve McClaren, who is the club's director of football, as well as head coach Alex Bruce and the coaching staff.

Brandon Williams joins Rotherham United

A statement read: "The 26-year-old officially joins the Millers having worked hard throughout pre-season and into late October at the club’s Roundwood training base, where he has proven his fitness to Steve McClaren, Alex Bruce and the coaching staff.



"The Manchester-born full-back has an incredibly impressive pedigree having earned a place in the Manchester United first team setup after progressing through their illustrious Academy to earn his senior chance.

"Williams represented the Red Devils at the very highest level turning out in the Champions League, UEFA Europa League and Premier League, also making appearances in the top flight for Norwich City.



"More recently, the forward-thinking defender has turned out for Ipswich Town and Hull City at Sky Bet Championship level and can call upon experience with the England U20 and U21 age groups.

"Williams will wear the number 33 shirt for the Millers."

Williams has not appeared in a competitive game since August 2025, during his solitary appearance for Hull City in the Championship.



He departed the Tigers just six months into his one-year contract, having managed just a five-minute cameo in a 3-0 loss to Blackburn.

The last time Williams played a full 90 minutes was in November 2023 when he was on loan at Ipswich Town.

He is hoping to revive his football career after he was handed a suspended 14-month prison sentence for dangerous driving last year.

Williams, who has since expressed regret publicly for the ordeal, now looks to have his off-field issues behind him to join Rotherham.



Brandon Williams 'deserves' EFL contract

"I'm really pleased he's a Rotherham player," said boss Rotherham boss Bruce. "He deserves the contract.

"He's worked really, really hard with us since pre-season.

"He's shown a great attitude. He's shown an appetite and a hunger to come in every day without getting paid."

2 Williams has penned a deal that ties him to AESSEAL New York Stadium until January 23 Credit: Getty

"I think he's had to face the reality of that's where his life was at," Bruce continued. "I know Brandon from my connections to the Manchester area. I've come across him a few times. I know people who've worked with him at Man United as teammates and coaches.



"Steve McClaren and Richard Hartis know him as well.

"He looks a hell of a lot better than what he did when he first arrived for pre-season, that's for sure. Let's hope he can kick on now, and he can be an asset to the club.

"Let's not lose sight of where he's been and what kind of career he's had, even though he's still a young lad.

"I'm really pleased to give him the opportunity to hopefully kick-start his career."

Sports.title: Tearful Simone Biles struggles to come to terms with quick sale of $1M mansion she shared with NFL star husband
Sports.content:
Simone Biles broke down in tears as she said an emotional goodbye to her stunning Texas home where she spent six years alongside NFL star husband Jonathan Owens.

The 29-year-old took to TikTok to share the bittersweet moment with fans after the 3,998sq ft property was snapped up just four days after hitting the market.

'Why the f*** am I boohoo crying? F***,' Biles said through tears as she panned around the empty residence.

'This house will be on the market for the first time and I don't know why I'm boohoo crying. I was here for six years and I feel like there were so many good memories.

'I feel like I grew up in this house. It's made me a real adult so I'm going to miss it. Ugh, I didn't think I'd be emotional about a house', the gymnastics icon added.

Biles walked through the vacant rooms before stepping outside to the spacious backyard before sharing a warm message for the future homeowners.

Simone Biles broke down in tears as she said an emotional goodbye to her Texas home

The 29-year-old took to TikTok to share the bittersweet moment with fans after the 3,998-square-foot property was snapped up just four days after hitting the market

'Whoever buys this house, I hope it brings you as much joy as it did for me', she said.

Biles captioned the video: “I was so excited to put in air fresheners for the potential buyers & showing Jonathan the last look. I just cried instead… anyone else?”

The property was initially listed for $1.275 million before eventually being sold for a fee between $1.08 million and $1.24 million, according to the Houston Association of Realtors.

Spanning nearly 4,000sq ft in a gated community near Spring, Texas, the four-bedroom, 3.5-bathroom estate sits on just over an acre of land.

The luxury residence features a heated backyard swimming pool, an in-home sauna, a dedicated dog-washing station and a custom wine display wall.

Inside, the home boasts a waterfall island kitchen with quartz countertops, a hidden walk-in pantry and an oversized three-car garage.

The property went under contract just four days after the listing went live on September 22, with the sale officially closing on October 15.

The gymnastics icon spent six years in the home alongside NFL star husband Jonathan Owens

Earlier this year, Biles shared a glimpse at the stunning property in a series of online posts

The update comes one month after Biles revealed three masked intruders broke into her Chicago home and stole her luxurious Porsche.

The legendary Team USA gymnast dropped the bombshell news during a TikTok video. It remains unclear when the burglary happened or if the police have made any arrests but Biles confirmed the car was recovered.

'Feel like I need a new car because during our last few months in Chicago, three men in masks came to our house and stole my Porsche,' she said.

'Stole the GTS. But that's another story. If you guys want to know, I'll do a story time on that.'

Sports.title: How Enzo Maresca stepped out of Pep Guardiola's shadow at Man City: 'Fire' in his team talks, heart-to-hearts with Phil Foden, rejecting old boss' office and a new attacking philosophy
Sports.content:
Stalking the room, Enzo Maresca is demanding answers. Demanding to know that his message is seeping in, demanding his players answer in the affirmative.

Maresca commands the space, down on his haunches complaining about Manchester City’s attitude towards second balls and defending. He’s loud, possesses what modern-day managers describe as ‘fire’ and players do not allow their gaze to divert inside that dressing room haze.

The scene, from a team talk earlier this season, reminds you of somebody. Pep Guardiola might be gone but the process of replacing him had to lead City towards a successor who while his own man, carving his own way, does bear a reasonable resemblance. And no, not just physically.

This decision, taken by director of football Hugo Viana with the blessing of Txiki Begiristain – who championed Maresca’s cause more than anyone else – is one that needed to strike a balance of continuity and change. Maresca has moved the dial without new concepts feeling completely alien. That’s the trick – a refresh, not reset.

Guardiola was back in town last week, far earlier than expected after waving a teary goodbye in May. The seismic guilty verdicts accelerated a return, as Guardiola sat in the directors’ box for the defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and had a debrief with Maresca in the inner sanctum afterwards.

Once it was security green-lighting requests for Noel Gallagher to enter the area around the dressing room to see Guardiola and now it was the same staff doing it for Guardiola himself.

Enzo Maresca has moved the dial at Manchester City after Pep Guardiola's exit without new concepts feeling completely alien

The Italian has led City to seven wins from seven to begin the Premier League season

Maresca is not in constant contact with his predecessor, as he has reiterated on a number of occasions. They spoke following the emotional one-goal victory at Old Trafford last month but Guardiola is mindful of staying out of the way and thought long and hard before accepting the invite for PSG, fearing his appearance might prove a distraction.

Given the pair are close, Maresca the assistant during the Treble campaign, the situation must be taking some getting used to.

Guardiola is watching City at home religiously and, more pertinently, paying close attention to the fallout of the guilty verdicts handed down for serious breaches of financial rules that could see the club relegated to the Championship, pending an appeal.

He will have noticed the consummate way in which Maresca handled the scrutiny in media briefings, with an authoritative charm and dry humour. A slight detachment certainly helps – something Guardiola could not have utilised were he still in the chair, where the exchanges would likely have been considerably more adversarial.

The way a sanguine Maresca addressed the charges with the players, ‘we have a title to win’ and ‘let’s make our own noise’, was designed to insulate the squad from a hurricane of comment and censure.

In 2023 when the charges dropped, Guardiola used it as fuel. No one likes us and all that. Clearly both styles have their merits and the one three years ago kickstarted a phenomenal run ending in Istanbul.

Maresca was a picture of relaxation as he flicked through his phone while leaning on the Etihad’s breeze blocks down the tunnel on Tuesday night after hammering AEK Athens 5-1. Guardiola looked identical, propped on exactly the same spot hundreds of times before.

Maresca is content at the start, surprised at the consistency of results – City will attempt to go eight from eight in the Premier League at Aston Villa on Saturday – and knows there is room for serious improvement.

Maresca is content at the start, surprised at the consistency of results and knows there is room for serious improvement

Guardiola is mindful of staying out of the way and thought long and hard before accepting the invite for the PSG game, fearing his appearance might prove a distraction

‘When you lose important players, many important players, and you lose the manager after 10 years, it always takes time to compete again,’ Maresca said, referencing the exits of Rodri, John Stones, Bernardo Silva, Nathan Ake, Manuel Akanji and more. ‘But we are competing at the moment. This is already a great achievement. We want more.’

There is a degree of pride in that statement from a man who is aware of the need to change certain bits of day-to-day life at the City Football Academy and how they tactically go about winning trophies – for however long that remains a possibility.

So keen is Maresca to subtly alter the messaging that instead of assuming Guardiola’s office he moved to one down the hall. He’s held heart-to-heart conversations with Phil Foden in a bid to recapture his form, with the previous boss having once visited the academy graduate’s house for similar reasons.

Undoubtedly, the 46-year-old wants a more aggressive City. A City more in the image of the 2018 Centurions than the Treble winners. An invitation for the wingers to go at their markers with more regularity, owning their individualism, and the general sense of attempting to force the ball into the box for Erling Haaland with added urgency.

Players keep saying that the messaging is clear – even if Maresca claimed recently that he’d rather win 1-0 than the basketball 5-3 against Sunderland, which is a position at odds with their swashbuckling performances. ‘I think we can attack better, we can defend better,’ Maresca said. ‘It's a matter of finding balance.’

While Maresca bristled at suggestions they gave up a few too many chances when beating Ipswich Town, the 4-2 home defeat by PSG a few days earlier gave stronger answers on the balancing act.

He talks about needing the build-up to sharpen up – meaning more control and retaining midfield stability – and removing Rayan Cherki at half-time for teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi when three down offered that.

The midfield trio of Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez appeared more symmetrical and could represent a blueprint in the tougher games – especially away from home.

Maresca has held heart-to-heart conversations with Phil Foden in a bid to recapture his form

He wants control and balance in midfield, exemplified by bringing on Ayyoub Bouaddi at 3-0 down to PSG and getting a foothold

‘One of the best in Europe in the right position,' Maresca said of Rayan Cherki. 'I also like simple things. I think the most difficult thing in football is to do easy things, don't complicate.’

The Cherki flicks and tricks were mesmeric in midweek against AEK, with another spectacular goal to boot. ‘Top player,’ Maresca said. ‘One of the best players in Europe when he is in the right position. I also like simple things. I think the most difficult thing in football is to do the easy things, don't complicate.’

We’ve definitely heard those words before, delivered from the same seat last season. Maresca says he learnt more from PSG than any other game and some of that will be down to the mentality of his leaders from the break onwards. The second-half dominance, when City created scores of opportunities, taught him something tactically but also about the fortitude of certain players.

‘We don’t like to lose games, but the mood in the dressing room afterwards was very positive,’ he said. ‘The players can see with their eyes that if we compete in the way we did in the second half, we are there. It was a nice feeling because yes, we lost the game, but we can be there, we are there.’

Again, that sort of summation sounds familiar. And that is definitely no bad thing for City. Just don’t call him Diet Pep. Somebody tried that once and it didn’t end well. This is Enzo Max.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola feels 'lucky' to be coaching Liverpool prodigy Rio Ngumoha but warns against putting 'impossible demands' on 18-year-old
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola feels 'lucky' to be coaching Liverpool prodigy Rio Ngumoha but warns against putting 'impossible demands' on 18-year-old

Andoni Iraola says he feels lucky to coach Liverpool starlet Rio Ngumoha – but has urged people to not expect too much too soon from the 18-year-old.

Ngumoha received rave reviews on Tuesday night with a spell-binding performance against Villarreal, in which he made two goals with mazy runs, and Reds boss Iraola is loving it.

Iraola, whose side play Brighton in a top-of-the-table tussle on Sunday, insists Ngumoha is not fazed by the hype.

‘Rio is very coachable,’ he said. ‘He pays attention, he listens to every information we give.

‘We haven't done anything super special with him. It's like let's give him confidence, continue the process and he is the one adding a lot to his game.

‘I haven't felt that he's very affected, positively or negatively, by the things (pundits and media) talk about him.

Andoni Iraola (right) says he feels fortunate to be managing Rio Ngumoha (left)

'I think he's very focused on the football side, of improving his performances, of trying to get the things that we need from him.

‘It's not easy when you are 18 and everyone is talking about you, but he knows that what matters is what is happening today in training, the things that he can add to his game, and I think he's very focused there.

‘Definitely, I feel lucky to have him, but I think there is also a moment where we cannot also, just because he has played well, put the expectation straight away super high because it's not fair for him.

‘Because he will still make mistakes, he will have his moments up and down, and this is a natural process that every player goes through. So we cannot straight away put the demands in Rio that are impossible to beat.’

A yellow weather warning is issued around Anfield on Sunday which the authorities are keeping an eye on.

Liverpool will be without winger Victor Munoz and vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai but Bradley Barcola has returned to training after missing some sessions this week.

Sports.title: Ric Flair rushed to hospital in ambulance hours after WWE legend canceled appearance due to blood clots
Sports.content:
Wrestling legend Ric Flair has been rushed to a Florida hospital shortly after canceling an appearance due to blood clots.

The 77-year-old born Richard Morgan Fliehr was at a Tampa restaurant on Friday morning, according to a report by TMZ. Flair is said to have stood up from the bar, leaving his phone and drink behind, before walking across the street and falling. TMZ further reports that Flair cut his face and the area around his eye, adding that he may have suffered a concussion.

He was taken into an ambulance and rushed to a nearby hospital.

The Daily Mail has sought comment from a Flair spokesperson.

Only hours earlier, Flair released a statement saying he would not be attending a fan convention in Seattle on the advice of his doctors, who are worried about some recently discovered blood clots.

'Blood Clots Are Extremely Serious And Can Be Life-Threatening,' Flair wrote online, capitalizing the first letter of every word. 'We Have Seen This Recently With [Philadelphia Eagles quarterback] Jalen Hurts And The Complications Involving Blood Clots In His Lungs. It Is A Reminder That This Is Not Something To Take Lightly, And I Must Follow Medical Advice.'

Wrestling legend Ric Flair (pictured here in 2025) has been rushed to a Florida hospital shortly after canceling an appearance due to blood clots

Ric Flair posted a photo of himself outside of an emergency room back in May

The 77-year-old born Richard Morgan Fliehr was at a Tampa restaurant on Friday morning, according to a report by TMZ. Flair is said to have walked across the street before collapsing

Flair said he can resume traveling after he undergoes a procedure on the affected vein.

He previously revealed a skin cancer battle in 2025, as well as unspecified health issues back in May.

'If you understood the health issues that I deal with and am currently dealing with, you would understand why I get frustrated in life with a lot of people,' he wrote online at the time. 'I'm sorry for the frustration. I am taking time to focus on my health.'

Flair also revealed a legal battle with his family.

In a series of since-deleted posts, the 'Nature Boy' claimed there is 'someone that I'm very familiar with' who is using 'my own trademark, FLAIR.'

He warned them that he is 'well represented by a reputable $1,000 per-hour attorney' who 'makes a living suing people that abuse my trademark.'

Flair is known for his years across the WWF/WWE, the WCW and other wrestling promotions.

Sports.title: Max Verstappen fumes at 'unacceptable' Austin track for US Grand Prix: Red Bull star warns track is 'out of control' and insists drivers' concerns have been IGNORED
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen fumes at 'unacceptable' Austin track for US Grand Prix: Red Bull star warns track is 'out of control' and insists drivers' concerns have been IGNORED

Max Verstappen has said that the ‘unacceptable’ Austin track, home of this weekend’s US Grand Prix, is damaging his spine because it is too bumpy.

The four-time world champion revealed that he and his fellow drivers have complained to the governing FIA about the condition of the Circuit of the Americas layout and asked for solutions but reported that their requests had not been resolved.

He described the circuit, which is 15 miles southeast of Downtown, as ‘out of control’.

‘I love this track, I love this place,’ said the Dutchman. ‘It’s one of the best, one of the best venues, one of the best cities to be at.

‘But the bumps are unacceptable. Over time they’ve found a bit of a solution here and there, but it’s just putting a plaster on the bigger problem.

‘You need to open up the track fully (to sort it out). That costs a lot of money and time but that’s the only way to get rid of it because these bumps are not natural.’

Max Verstappen has complained about the Austin track ahead of the US Grand Prix

The circuit, which hosted its first race 14 years ago, is built on marshland, and was designed by German Hermann Tilke, then the go-to man for such projects.

Verstappen, 29, added: ‘You can say soil is the problem, but you need to make sure you reinforce it more.’

Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli, just 20, can win the title here in the US if he extends his lead from 102 points to 125 with what would then be five rounds remaining.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany rushed to hospital in an ambulance after collapsing at Bayern Munich's training ground: Reserve team players left 'shaken' as Man City lead messages of support
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany rushed to hospital in an ambulance after collapsing at Bayern Munich's training ground: Reserve team players left 'shaken' as Man City lead messages of support

Vincent Kompany has been taken to hospital after collapsing while watching Bayern Munich's second team train on Friday.

Kompany, 40, has been suffering from a viral infection which is said to have caused problems with old scar tissue in his hip, leaving him in pain and with difficulties climbing stairs.

BILD report that a 'rescue helicopter' had landed at Bayern's training ground on Friday. The former captain of Manchester City, who won four Premier League titles, later went to hospital in an ambulance and is said to be in a stable condition.

Kompany had collapsed as he watched the club's second string. He had earlier taken training for the first team ahead of their Bundesliga clash against Freiburg on Sunday.

The session was then abandoned, BILD said, with those present said to be 'deeply affected' by the incident.

He had been spectating with Bayern II's new coach, Dante, 43, before collapsing 20 minutes into the session. It is understood that most players were back in the changing rooms when the incident occurred but those who witnessed it were shaken, and the reserve team's game against DJK Vilzing on Saturday has been called off.

Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital by ambulance from Bayern Munich's training ground

Kompany is pictured with his wife Carla at Oktoberfest in Munich last month

Kompany's viral infection caused issues with his hip that left him struggling to stand for long periods of time and was thoroughly examined by team medical staff earlier in the week and was given a pill by one of the doctors early on in the game against Arsenal.

Bayern said in a statement: 'Vincent Kompany had to seek medical treatment on Friday after collapsing during training for FC Bayern's amateurs.

'The first-team coach had been watching the second team's session. Kompany will undergo thorough examination in the hospital and remain in medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage training and match operations.'

Bayern's sporting director, Max Eberl, added: 'The health of Vincent Kompany is our utmost priority. At FC Bayern, we will do everything to ensure he recovers quickly.

'Vinnie is receiving all necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs. His coaching team, which we fully trust, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery.'

Kompany's former club Manchester City were among those to send a message of support to the Belgian following the incident. City wrote on X: 'Everyone at Manchester City is wishing a speedy recovery to our former captain and Club legend, Vincent Kompany. Get well soon, Vinny.'

After the 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, Kompany said: 'As a coach, you always want to do everything and accomplish everything. I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body, and then at some point my body said, "Stop now!"'

Kompany had missed training sessions and a press conference in the build-up to the Arsenal game but was present on the touchline on the night.

He also watched Bayern's previous game, a 6-1 win against RB Leipzig, from the bench but did not conduct interviews afterwards.

The Belgian was captain of Man City during some of their most successful years under Pep Guardiola but was regularly ruled out through injuries.

Kompany moved to Munich in 2024 and has won two Bundesliga titles with England captain Harry Kane as his star player in attack. He has three children with wife Carla, who he met in Manchester.

His viral infection was the talk of the build-up before Wednesday's Champions League match.

Everyone at Manchester City is wishing a speedy recovery to our former captain and Club legend, Vincent Kompany.



Get well soon, Vinny 🩵 https://t.co/RYUP7DjYkj pic.twitter.com/fozzCkHGQl — Manchester City (@ManCity) October 23, 2026

Kompany's assistant coach Aaron Danks said on Tuesday: 'It has affected his legs, yes. He has had pain in his legs.

'The most important thing for him now is to rest and I don't know if he will be ready tomorrow or in two or three days' time.

'Getting him to rest is hard. He's a leader. But it's a virus and it's really important that he rests.'

Bayern are top of Germany's Bundesliga after four wins and two draws in their opening six matches. They lie 14th in the Champions League's league phase after a win and two draws.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso sends warning to Chelsea stars ahead of crunch Spurs clash as Blues boss aims to avoid repeat of infamous Battle of the Bridge
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso has ordered his Chelsea players to keep calm and carry on by not spoiling their vastly-improved disciplinary record when they take on their arch rivals Tottenham Hotspur. August, September and October last season saw Chelsea receive six red cards in all competitions, including one for then-manager Enzo Maresca. This term, Alonso's side have yet to drop down to 10 men with the Spaniard revealing how he purposefully sought to fix this problem after arriving. One way in which the Blues boss achieved that was by signing Jordan Henderson, the 36-year-old who could now complete a fourth consecutive full 90 when he starts against Spurs. Alonso credited Henderson with adding to the 'emotional control' that the team needed as they dive into a derby which will forever conjure memories of the 2016 Battle of the Bridge. 'We could do better,' Alonso said when asked about Chelsea's red-led previous season which contributed to them finishing 10th and missing out on European qualification. 'For me it comes a lot with emotional control, with the control of the game. If you are focused on what you have to do, you are prepared for what's going on. Normally you don't make that many mistakes and you don't overreact to certain situations. Xabi Alonso ordered his Chelsea players to keep calm and carry on by not spoiling their vastly-improved disciplinary record 'For me this is a fundamental part of the game, to have that emotional control, to deal with all this. The momentum is coming, we keep calm, I don't lose my head and I don't get stupid yellow cards or make stupid penalties. You need to prepare for football to have better control of that.' Liam Delap, Robert Sanchez and Trevoh Chalobah were among those red carded in the first three months of last season, and, along with Maresca, they are now not with Chelsea. Alonso and Henderson arrived in the summer, and the manager said on his midfielder: 'Absolutely it helps. Absolutely. It helps for that experience and that composure that you need in certain moments. You have players that sometimes, even during the game, they take a step back to see this is happening and now we need to keep focused and calm.' It is not easy when the Premier League is full of fans who love seeing hard tackles, aggro between opponents, and end-to-end football. 'It is really difficult,' Alonso conceded. 'You know that if you concede one, the energy is coming, and you need to control the momentum. You can have a mental preparation. You need to have composure to deal with those moments. 'To say "Come on guys, we know what we have to do, we have prepared for this and the other moment will come' for me is fundamental." That is from the people on the pitch. 'We are expecting a good atmosphere, electric, with good energy, knowing that in a derby this passion is really in the air in the stadium. We need to use it in a proper way because this is all about those games where you feel that excitement.' Mike Penders will make his first Premier League start in goal with Emiliano Martinez sidelined. Alonso backed the 21-year-old to handle the pressure and compared him to Thibaut Courtois. Chelsea's manager added he phoned the Real Madrid goalkeeper in the summer to receive intel on his Belgian compatriot Penders, saying: 'Thibaut even said himself that he could see resemblances with Mike.'
