World.title: 2027: Kwankwaso pledges jobs, security, education as Obi misses Plateau meeting
World.content:
Rabiu Kwankwaso, the vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has pledged that a government led by the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, would prioritise security, education, agriculture and job creation if elected in 2027.

Mr Kwankwaso made the pledge on Friday at a town hall meeting with stakeholders in Jos, Plateau State, where he described the Obi–Kwankwaso ticket as a platform for national unity.

Mr Obi was absent from the meeting, which brought together party leaders, supporters, civil society groups and journalists.

Kwankwaso explains Obi’s absence

Mr Kwankwaso said Mr Obi called him earlier on Friday to explain that circumstances beyond his control had prevented him from travelling to Plateau State.

According to him, Mr Obi asked him to assure Plateau residents of the ticket’s commitment to the state and promised that both candidates would return for another engagement.

“His Excellency Peter Obi told me to inform you that, together, we are 100 per cent with the good people of Plateau State,” Mr Kwankwaso said.

He added that the candidates had agreed to harmonise their visions for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This ticket is a ticket of unity — unity in Plateau, unity in Northern Nigeria, unity in Southern Nigeria, and unity in Nigeria,” he said.

Kwankwaso decries killings, poverty

The former Kano State governor and minister of defence identified insecurity, poverty, hunger, unemployment and the decline of industries as some of Nigeria’s most pressing challenges.

He criticised what he described as the apparent indifference of political leaders to recurring killings across the country, whether arising from banditry, insurgency or communal violence.

“You wake up and 20 people, 100 people or even more are killed like chickens, and nobody cares,” he said. “Human beings are human beings. We have to have caring leaders in this country.”

Mr Kwankwaso argued that any administration unable to protect citizens and uphold their dignity should not be rewarded with another term.

Candidate promises education reforms

Mr Kwankwaso pledged that an Obi-led administration would expand access to education, particularly in northern Nigeria.

Citing his record as governor of Kano State, he said his administration provided opportunities for school-age children to attend primary school and enabled qualified pupils to proceed to secondary and tertiary institutions.

He called for the extension of similar opportunities across the country, including Plateau State, which he described as sharing cultural and demographic similarities with Kano.

Pledges jobs, agricultural support

Mr Kwankwaso said the decline of industries and factories had deprived many communities, including those in Plateau, of employment opportunities, leaving many young people without reliable sources of livelihood.

He said the proposed administration would focus on reviving agriculture, supporting farmers and creating jobs for young Nigerians.

“The shoes we had in the past are gone, and nobody cares,” he said, referring to the decline of local manufacturing.

He did not provide specific targets for job creation or details of how the proposed administration would finance the promised programmes.

Kwankwaso urges voters to protect ballots

Mr Kwankwaso urged Plateau residents to support the Obi–Kwankwaso ticket on the NDC platform in the 2027 presidential election and ensure that their votes were protected.

“You have to start and protect those votes. You have done it before; try to do it again,” he said, referring to the political support the state gave Mr Obi in the 2023 presidential election.

He thanked the Middle Belt Forum, party supporters and journalists for attending the meeting, adding that the party’s leadership in Plateau would be contacted to arrange another visit by both candidates.

Opposition unity ahead of 2027

The Jos meeting comes amid continuing efforts by opposition politicians to build an alliance ahead of the 2027 general election.

Mr Kwankwaso has previously rejected calls to step aside for the African Democratic Congress (ADC) or another opposition platform, underscoring disagreements over the choice of a common presidential candidate.

The differences have raised questions about the prospects of opposition unity ahead of the election, despite discussions among political figures on the need to coordinate their efforts against the ruling party.

World.title: APC denies alliance with Bauchi governor but invites him to join party
World.content:
The Bauchi State Chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has debunked rumours of a political alliance with Governor Bala Mohammed, saying no political agreement exists between the party and the governor outside the official APC platform.

In a press statement issued by its state publicity secretary, Shehu Dauda, the party described claims of an understanding as baseless and urged the public to treat such reports with caution unless supported by credible evidence.

The APC noted Governor Mohammed’s continued association with and campaigning alongside candidates of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), including its presidential candidate.

According to the party, the activities contradict any claims of a political arrangement with the ruling party at the national level.

While acknowledging Governor Mohammed’s recent appreciation of President Bola Tinubu’s leadership, economic reforms, and health sector interventions, the APC urged him to end his political association with the APM and formally cross over to the APC.

“If the governor genuinely wishes to align Bauchi State with the federal government’s development agenda, joining the APC would provide a clear and consistent political platform for cooperation, coordination, and the advancement of the interests of the people of Bauchi State,” the statement read.

The party stated that Bauchi State is too strategic to remain outside Nigeria’s mainstream political alignment, noting that joining the APC would enhance state-federal collaboration, attract more development opportunities, and improve citizens’ access to federal programmes.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Reaffirming its commitment to President Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, the Bauchi APC urged residents of the state to remain calm, discerning, and focused on good governance, unity, and development.

World.title: Trump lifts some Canada tariffs ahead of midterms
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump. Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP.

President Donald Trump’s administration lifted some tariffs on Canadian imports Friday, two weeks ahead of midterm elections, after a vulnerable Republican candidate said she’d lobbied for the change.

The easing of tariffs will apply to products including “plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment,” the White House said in a statement.

The change could help Senator Susan Collins, who faces a strong challenge from a Democrat in the US-Canada border state of Maine, which has been hit hard by Trump’s trade war.

She posted on social media that she had “secured” the exemptions for “products crucial to Maine’s agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers.”

Democrats are targeting Collins’s seat in their attempt to win control of Congress from the Republicans in the November 3 midterms.

The economies of the United States and Canada are heavily inter-connected, with roughly 70 percent of all Canadian exports heading to the United States.

Tensions between the North American neighbors have been high since trade talks broke down in August, with Trump imposing a slew of new tariffs in response.

Friday’s action lifts tariffs on certain goods, but imposes levies on new ones, including carpets, certain valves and waste products, the White House said. The new measures will take effect on October 30.

Collins said many farmers in her state “rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense.”

Previous Trump levies on autos, steel, aluminum and lumber have hit Canada hard, forcing job losses and stunting growth. Canada has entered a technical recession this year after two consecutive quarters of economic contraction.

Trump’s tariffs enforced after the talks broke down impacted around $20 billion worth of goods, or 5.5 percent of Canadian exports to the United States, targeting products ranging from hockey sticks to cement.

Since taking power in his second term, Trump has upended the global trade order by imposing wide-ranging tariffs on friend and foe alike, saying that other countries have been taking advantage of the United States.

He has also explicitly tied some threatened tariffs to political or foreign policy objectives.

World.title: Nigeria’s first Ebola case ‘highly similar’ to Kenyan one – Minister
World.content:
Genomic tests have shown that the Ebola virus found in Nigeria’s first case resembles that of the first case recorded in Kenya earlier this month, Nigeria’s health minister said Friday.

Nigeria announced its first Ebola case on Tuesday, the wife of a staff member at Switzerland’s embassy in Abuja, who had returned from Uganda on October 3.

She had not visited the Democratic Republic of Congo — the epicentre of the current outbreak, the Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday, contrary to earlier reports by the Ugandan government.

Health authorities on the continent have been trying to trace the source of her infection — with Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention earlier suggesting she may have come into contact at the airport with Kenya’s first patient, who also flew from Uganda on the same day.

Based on the the genomic analysis, the case in Nigeria “appears to be closely related to the case identified in the index case in Kenya”, Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate told reporters.

“There is no evidence of travel of that index case in Kenya that links it to Nigeria, but the viruses are appearing to be related,” he said, adding in a post on X that the case “is highly similar to that from Kenya”.

Following the DRC, Uganda and Kenya, Nigeria has become the fourth African country to be affected by the Bundibugyo species outbreak.

After flaring up in the northeastern DRC in May, the deadly viral haemorrhagic fever spread into neighbouring Uganda, where 20 confirmed cases, including two deaths were recorded before the outbreak there was officially over in August.

To date, the epidemic has surpassed 9,700 confirmed cases, including 4,690 deaths, according to WHO figures as of October 20.

World.title: Xenophobia: FG condemns attacks, evacuates 114 more Nigerians from South Africa
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Favour Ulebor, Abuja

The Federal Government has condemned xenophobic and Afrophobic hostilities against Nigerians and other foreign nationals in South Africa, as it evacuated another 114 distressed citizens from the country.

In a statement on Friday evening, the latest batch of returnees comprised 57 men, 23 women and 34 children who arrived in Lagos aboard South African Airways Flight SA060 at about 8:30 p.m. on Thursday, October 22, 2026.

The returnees were received by officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the National Emergency Management Agency, the Nigeria Immigration Service and other relevant Federal Government agencies.

The ministry said the latest operation was the 16th consular evacuation since the exercise began on June 10, 2026, bringing the total number of Nigerians evacuated from South Africa to 2,151.

It explained that the Redeemed Christian Church of God, RCCG, under the leadership of Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, funded the one-way tickets for the latest batch from its $265,854 donation to support the evacuation of 500 distressed Nigerians.

With the latest evacuation, the church has funded the return of 432 Nigerians, while the Federal Government has fully funded the evacuation of 1,388 citizens.

The Federal Government expressed appreciation to the RCCG for its financial support towards the humanitarian exercise.

Condemning the attacks, the government called on the relevant South African authorities to take decisive measures to protect all persons, irrespective of nationality, and ensure that perpetrators of violence against foreign nationals are held accountable.

It said it would continue engaging relevant stakeholders, including South African authorities, to address xenophobia and Afrophobia and promote the safety and welfare of Nigerians residing in South Africa.

The statement in parts, “The latest operation marks the sixteenth (16th) consular evacuation since the commencement of the ongoing exercise on 10th June, 2026, bringing the total number of Nigerian nationals evacuated from South Africa to 2,151. Of this number, the Federal Government of Nigeria fully funded the return of 1,388 nationals.

“The Federal Government reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of all forms of xenophobic and Afrophobic hostilities directed at foreign nationals, including Nigerians, in South Africa. It further calls on the relevant South African authorities to take decisive measures to protect all persons, irrespective of nationality, and ensure that perpetrators of violence against foreign nationals are held accountable.

“While sustaining engagement with relevant stakeholders, including South African authorities, to address xenophobia and Afrophobia and promote the safety and welfare of Nigerians residing in South Africa, the Federal Government advises Nigerians in the country to abide by local laws, remain vigilant and prioritise personal safety.”

The government also advised Nigerians in the country to obey local laws, remain vigilant and prioritise their personal safety.

It urged them to maintain regular contact with the Nigerian High Commission in Pretoria and the Consulate General in Johannesburg for consular assistance whenever necessary.

The Federal Government reaffirmed its commitment to safeguarding Nigerians in the diaspora and providing timely consular assistance as the need arises.

World.title: 2027: You’ll win Benue by landslide  – Onjeh tells Obi
World.content:
The 2027 Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Benue South Senatorial Candidate, Comrade Daniel Onjeh, has told the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, that he expects him to win Benue State by a landslide in the 2027 presidential election.

Onjeh said this when he led a delegation of Benue State NDC National Assembly candidates on a strategic visit to the former Anambra State Governor.

Asked about the purpose of the visit, Onjeh said the delegation had gone to meet Obi to review what happened in the 2023 presidential election, look at the political situation in Benue and discuss what lies ahead in 2027.

He described Obi’s performance in Benue State during the 2023 presidential election as impressive and outstanding, adding that he expects the former Anambra State Governor to receive even greater support in 2027.

Onjeh said the delegation also discussed the state’s voting strength and the interest being shown in voter registration. He maintained that the support Obi received in 2023 reflected a desire for political change among sections of the electorate.

The former President of the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) said the delegation also appealed to Obi to make Benue State a priority, especially after what he described as the deliberate obstruction of his previous attempts to visit the state.

Onjeh questioned why a Nigerian citizen should be prevented from travelling freely within his own country, describing such interference as unacceptable.

He said the candidates encouraged Obi to put those experiences behind him and assured him that the concerns previously raised to stop his visits would be adequately addressed.

They also urged him to return and complete his humanitarian mission to Benue and spend sufficient time with the people during his proposed presidential campaign tour.

Obi, according to Onjeh, assured the delegation that Benue remained dear to his heart and that he would return to spend ample time with the people.

He said the former Anambra State Governor spoke about equity and justice, stressing that no part of Nigeria should be left out of his engagements with the people.

Beyond the discussions about Benue, Onjeh said Obi had an important message for the National Assembly candidates: they must prepare, organise themselves and their supporters, and ensure that the votes cast by Nigerians are protected.

He explained that Obi placed particular emphasis on the need for Nigerians not only to vote but also to ensure that their votes count.

According to Onjeh, Obi linked this to the country’s future, arguing that unless Nigerians can freely choose their leaders and have those choices respected, the country will continue to struggle with poverty and the other challenges holding back its development.

He said Obi also spoke about the need for Nigeria to make progress in technology and other sectors, noting that credible elections and accountable leadership were essential to moving the country forward.

Onjeh, a former Chairman of the Governing Board of the Projects Development Institute (PRODA), Enugu, said the meeting also allowed the Benue candidates to discuss their preparations and exchange views with Obi on developments in the state.

The former President of the West African Students’ Union (WASU) said the delegation left with a clear message about the importance of preparing early, working together and ensuring that voters are able to exercise their rights without interference.

He maintained that the 2027 election would provide another opportunity for the people of Benue to make their choice through the ballot.

World.title: 2027: Unlike 2023, Kaduna votes now for Tinubu, Gov Sani declares
World.content:
Gov Uba Sani and President Bola Tinubu.

By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja

Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State has declared that the state will vote massively for President Bola Tinubu in the forthcoming election, as against what obtained in the 2023 presidential election.

He made the declaration while receiving the Support Groups Directorate of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC), led by a former Deputy Governor of Nasarawa State, Dr Silas Agara, at the Government House, Kaduna, after thousands of supporters took to the streets in a pre-election solidarity walk.

“Kaduna State will support President Tinubu and vote massively for him in recognition of his achievements. We encourage our supporters to remain united, peaceful and committed to engaging the people as we prepare for Saturday’s rally,” the governor said.

The pledge comes against the background of the 2023 presidential election, in which Tinubu came second in Kaduna State. The Peoples Democratic Party PDP candidate, Atiku Abubakar, won the state with 554,360 votes, carrying 14 local government areas. Tinubu polled 399,293 votes and carried only two LGAs, Birnin-Gwari and Sanga. Peter Obi of the Labour Party followed with 294,494 votes and carried seven LGAs, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party NNPP polled 92,969 votes.

Sani commended the support groups for their mobilisation efforts and stressed the importance of political participation, unity and sustained engagement with citizens.

“We welcome the support group leaders and members to Kaduna State. Your presence demonstrates your commitment to the political process and your willingness to engage citizens on the direction of our country. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has continued to pursue policies and programmes aimed at addressing Nigeria’s challenges and laying the foundation for sustainable development. We recognise the importance of the ongoing reforms and the need to communicate their objectives and impact to Nigerians”, he said.

The procession began around the Savannah Bank area and moved towards the Government House before returning to the APC Ciki da Waje State Secretariat.

Participants carried numerous flags bearing inscriptions in support of the president and displayed their enthusiasm through drumming and dancing.

Agara commended the governor for receiving the delegation and acknowledged the contributions of support group leaders and members to the mobilisation exercise.

“Today’s solidarity walk demonstrates our commitment to organising and coordinating support groups ahead of the campaign. We have brought together members from different groups to demonstrate unity of purpose and strengthen our collective participation in the political process,” he said.

He said the mobilisation was part of the directorate’s responsibility to ensure that support groups were organised, active and ready to participate in the campaign.

“We appreciate Governor Uba Sani for receiving us and providing an opportunity for engagement as we prepare for Saturday’s rally,” Agara added.

Other notable figures at the engagement included a former Deputy Governor of Niger State, Alhaji Ahmed Mohammed Ketso; a former Deputy Governor of Edo State, Philip Shaibu; the Minister of State for Works, Bello Muhammad Goronyo; the North-West Coordinator of the Support Group Directorate, Bafa Dan Agundi; and Senator Suleiman Hunkuyi.

The convener said similar walks would be held in every state of the federation before each presidential rally. According to Agara, the work of the support groups did not end with the procession.

“Our task goes beyond carrying flags and participating in processions. We must engage citizens, communicate the policies and programmes of the administration, and ensure that Nigerians understand the issues at stake. We are determined to work together, strengthen our structures and sustain our mobilisation efforts ahead of the elections,” he said.

World.title: Naira depreciates to N1,367/$ in parallel market
World.content:
*Interbank turnover rises 219%

By Elizabeth Adegbesan

The naira today depreciated to N1,367 per dollar from N1,363 in the parallel market on Thursday.

Similarly, the naira depreciated to N1,370 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market, NFEM.

Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, showed that the indicative exchange rate for the naira rose to N1,370 per dollar from N1,365 per dollar on Thursday, indicating N5 depreciation for the naira.

Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets widened to N3 per dollar from N2 per dollar on Thursday.

The value of interbank turnover in NFEM increased by 219 per cent to $1.01 billion from $316.6 million on Thursday.

However, financial analysts expect the naira to remain depreciated.

In their weekly financial review and outlook, analysts at Cowry Asset Management said: “Going forward, the naira is expected to remain under pressure amid persistent demand for foreign exchange and prevailing market uncertainties, although the modest increase in external reserves could provide some support for currency stability.”

World.title: Police arrest suspect over murder of retired Ogun teacher
World.content:
police badge

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Ogun State Police Command has arrested a suspect in connection with the murder of a 61-year-old retired teacher, Mrs Adedotun Adeteju Oluwaseun, who was found dead at her residence in Agbaakin Emere, Bode-Olude, Abeokuta.

The suspect, identified as Alhaji Saburi Lateef Ayinde, popularly known as “Oki-Ocean”, was arrested on Monday, October 19, 2026, following investigations by detectives attached to the Homicide Section of the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Eleweran, Abeokuta.

The command disclosed this in a statement issued on Friday by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, who said the arrest followed sustained investigative efforts into the killing.

According to the statement, the deceased’s body was discovered in the toilet of her residence on February 28, 2026, a day after she reportedly returned from a retirement celebration organised by her colleagues.

The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the retired teacher was allegedly strangled and attacked with a machete during an altercation with the suspect.

The statement added that the case was subsequently transferred to the Homicide Section of the SCID for further investigation, which led to the suspect’s arrest.

“The suspect reportedly confessed to the killing and linked the incident to financial dealings with the deceased,” the statement said.

It explained that the suspect allegedly claimed he had entrusted ₦3.45 million to the deceased for safekeeping, with an understanding that she would lend him ₦1.5 million to purchase another vehicle.

However, the police said detectives were still working to corroborate the suspect’s account and establish the full circumstances surrounding the killing.

The State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, commended the investigating officers for their persistence, professionalism and commitment, which he said had resulted in a breakthrough in the case.

Ojajuni reiterated the command’s resolve to investigate serious crimes diligently, ensure accountability and bring offenders to justice through lawful prosecution.

The police said the suspect would be charged in court upon the conclusion of the investigation.

The command also urged residents to resolve disputes through lawful means and promptly report criminal activities to the appropriate authorities.

It assured members of the public that credible information provided to the police would be treated professionally and acted upon.

World.title: Messi receives top Spanish award from heir to throne
World.content:
Spain’s Princess Leonor shakes hands with Argentine football legend Lionel Messi as she awards him the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sport during the 2026 Princess of Asturias Awards ceremony at the Campoamor theatre in Oviedo on October 23, 2026. (Photo by ANDER GILLENEA / AFP)

Lionel Messi received Spain’s most prestigious sports award on Friday in recognition of his glittering career and his work for disadvantaged children’s access to health and education.

The Argentine forward, 39, was named winner of the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports in June, with the jury hailing “the most successful footballer of all time” and his social work.

Dozens of fans wearing Argentina football shirts cheered and chanted Messi’s name as he arrived to the sound of bagpipes and drums at the ceremony in Oviedo, capital of the northern Spanish region of Asturias.

Messi collected a formal roll of parchment from Princess Leonor, the heir to the Spanish throne after whom the awards are named, who lauded his “unique career”.

“He turned the extraordinary into routine by reading the game and deciding on the most effective option in fractions of a second, while respecting the collective essence above ego,” Leonor said.

One of the greatest footballers of all time, Messi has won eight Ballon d’Or titles, a World Cup and dozens of trophies at club level.

He spent 21 years at Barcelona where he played in a side that dominated Spain and Europe under Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique.

After leaving the Catalan club in 2021, Messi spent two years at French giants Paris Saint-Germain and currently plays for Inter Miami in MLS.

Argentina’s all-time top goalscorer, assist provider and caps holder called time on his international career earlier this year after losing the World Cup final to Spain in New Jersey.

“The most important thing is to know how to lose and how to win,” Messi told an event with children in Oviedo on Thursday, saying that attitude was “fundamental” in football.

Founded in 1981, the Princess of Asturias Awards are the most prestigious in the Spanish-speaking world and come with prize money of 50,000 euros ($56,000).

They encompass the arts, sciences and sports and are handed out annually in honour of efforts to improve human coexistence, solidarity and global cooperation.

British author Julian Barnes, trailblazing US astronaut Christina Koch and punk star Patti Smith were among the other winners who received their prize on Friday.

Previous winners of the sports award include tennis greats Serena Williams and Rafael Nadal, marathon record-breaker Eliud Kipchoge and US skier Lindsey Vonn.

World.title: FG Secures Conviction of 653 Terrorists in Latest Mass Trial
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

The federal government has secured the conviction of 653 persons charged with offences bordering on acts of terrorism before the Federal High Court, Abuja.

Attorney General of the Federation (AGF) and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, made the disclosure on Friday, while speaking with journalists in Abuja.

Fagbemi, who gave the update while reviewing the progress of the trials, which is on its 11th phase, observed that 1,060 suspects were brought before the courts for trial, which is the third phase conducted this year.

He disclosed that as at noon on Friday, 880 cases had been tried, resulting in 653 convictions, seven acquittals and 27 discharges.

The AGF, however, said the exercise was still ongoing and that the final figures would be announced upon its conclusion, describing the current phase as apparently the largest, since the federal government commenced the special terrorism trials, attributing the progress to judicial cooperation, effective prosecution and inter-agency collaboration.

Fagbemi expressed appreciation to the judges handling the cases, particularly under the leadership of Justice Binta Nyako, who has been acting on behalf of the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho.

He also commended prosecution and defence counsel, as well as relevant security and justice institutions, for their contributions to the exercise.

Among the agencies acknowledged were the Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA), the Department of State Services (DSS), the military, the police, correctional centres and the Legal Aid Council.

Fagbemi noted that the collaboration among the institutions has been critical to advancing the prosecution of terrorism, terrorism financing and related offences in the country.

The AGF also thanked journalists for informing the public about the federal government’s efforts to address terrorism and related security challenges in the country.

On the representation of defendants by lawyers from the Legal Aid Council, the AGF explained that the council was fulfilling its responsibility of providing legal assistance to eligible defendants and clarified, however, that private legal practitioners were also representing some of the suspects.

According to him, defence lawyers had been engaging with their clients before the court proceedings, including visiting detention facilities and preparing them for their defence. He noted that some of these preparatory activities could not be subjected to public scrutiny because of the sensitive security considerations surrounding the cases.

On the issue of deradicalisation of suspects recommended by the court, Fagbemi said the process remained an important component of the overall exercise, explaining that deradicalisation was intended to help eligible individuals understand and regret their actions, enabling them to reintegrate into society and resume their daily lives.

The AGF maintained that rehabilitation and reintegration were necessary to complement the judicial process and reduce the risk of individuals returning to extremist activities.

The ongoing trials form part of the federal government’s efforts to prosecute terrorism-related offences and strengthen accountability in the country’s response to insecurity.

World.title: Daily Times Centenary to Spotlight Nigeria’s Development Challenges
World.content:
Daily Times Nigeria will convene policymakers, business leaders and other stakeholders in Lagos on November 3 to discuss Nigeria’s development priorities as the newspaper marks its centenary with a policy town hall, an archival exhibition and the DTN@100 Times Heroes Awards.

The event, scheduled for Harbour Point, Lagos, will focus on issues including informal employment, energy access, infrastructure, productive livelihoods and the conditions needed to attract investment and sustain economic growth.

Held under the theme “Honouring the Past, Shaping the Future,” the gathering will also recognise individuals and institutions whose contributions have influenced Nigeria’s political, economic, social and cultural development.

Chairman of the DTN@100 Times Heroes Awards Council, Bolaji Okusaga, said the centenary offered an opportunity to draw lessons from Nigeria’s history while encouraging a new generation to contribute to the country’s future.

“As Daily Times celebrates 100 years of documenting Nigeria’s journey, the DTN@100 Times Heroes Awards is an opportunity to honour the people and institutions whose vision, courage and contributions have helped shape our nation,” Okusaga said.

He added that the initiative was intended to preserve the lessons of the past, recognise present achievements and inspire efforts towards a more prosperous and inclusive Nigeria.

The Times Heroes Awards will honour individuals and institutions for their contributions to national development, including leadership, enterprise, public service, innovation and job creation.

Another feature of the centenary initiative is ‘The Nigerian Grand Book, National Book of Changemakers,’ a publication developed over 15 years and informed by the newspaper’s century-long archive. With a foreword by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the book will document the achievements of distinguished Nigerians, with each award recipient allocated a page to preserve their story for future generations.

The programme will also include the Honouring the Past Exhibition, which will draw on the Daily Times archive to revisit people, events and milestones that have shaped the country over the past century.

The initiative builds on an earlier gathering held on September 3, 2026, at THISDAY Dome, Abuja. The event attracted prominent national figures, including Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, who represented President Tinubu; Dr Akinwumi Adesina, who delivered the keynote address and received an award; Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu; and Governors Abdullahi Sule, Umar Bago and Dauda Lawal. Traditional rulers in attendance included the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, and the Obi of Onitsha, Igwe Nnaemeka Achebe.

Beyond recognising distinguished Nigerians, the organisers say the centenary initiative seeks to preserve national memory and deepen public understanding of the people and institutions behind the country’s development. The exhibition will also provide opportunities for schoolchildren to engage with Nigeria’s history, with a sponsorship model designed to support school attendance.

Founded a century ago, Daily Times has documented Nigeria’s political, economic, social and cultural evolution. As it enters its second century, the newspaper is using the milestone to revisit that history while creating a platform for conversations about the leadership, policies and partnerships needed to shape the country’s future.

World.title: Cross River Lauds DSS, Others For Intercepting 3 GPMGs, Cache of High-calibre Arms
World.content:
The Cross River government has lauded the Department of State Services (DSS) and sister security agencies for recently intercepting a huge cache of High-calibre weapons, which included three General Purpose Machine Guns (GPMGs).

The state Deputy Governor Rt. Hon. Peter Odey made the commendation on Friday after inspecting the seized weapons at the DSS state headquarters in Calabar.

Odey, whose visit was on behalf of Governor Bassey Otu, commended the Service on the intelligence operation that led to the seizure of the weapons which included seven A-K 47 assault rifles.

The deputy governor stated that the arrest of two suspected gunrunners during the operation, would help the DSS and sister security agencies apprehend those behind the illegal arms trade.

He noted that had the weapons not been intercepted, there was a strong possibility that it could be used to wreak havoc in the state and neighbouring states, particularly during the forthcoming general elections.

The deputy governor praised the growing synergy between the security agencies and the military, saying the development has helped the government increasingly turn the tide against criminal elements.

World.title: 24 State Houses Of Assembly Okay State Police Bill
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidency on Friday has expressed happiness as State Police Amendment Bill scales constitutional hurdle in 24 out of the 36 states of the federation.

Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon Femi Gbajabiamila, noted with satisfaction that the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, providing for a dual policing system, has been approved by 24 State Houses of Assembly, meeting the constitutional threshold of two-thirds of the 36 states.

Gbajabiamila, in a release,commended the State Houses of Assembly for their decisive action on this reform of national importance and appreciates the National Assembly for passing the amendment in both chambers.

According to him, in line with Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution, the amendment can now be returned to the National Assembly for transmission to Mr President for assent.

Gbajabiamila further said: “The approval gives constitutional backing to the policing framework that the Working Group’s draft National Policing Bill, 2026 is designed to implement.

“The Working Group’s efforts remain on track. The draft Bills are currently undergoing legislative drafting review and validation at the Federal Ministry of Justice and are expected to be returned on or before Friday, 30th October 2026. Thereafter, the Group will give them final consideration before presenting them to Mr President.

“The Working Group urges all stakeholders to support a smooth transition to a dual policing system that makes Nigerians safer.”

The Presidency had on Tuesday disclosed that the draft of the 2026 National Policing Bill is ready.

Gbajabiamila, stated in a release that the group has completed the drafting stage of its assignment and has formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), together with 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting review and validation.

According to him, the submission took place on Monday, 19th October, 2026, to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group’s work plan while the Ministry’s review will ensure that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions, and that they do not conflict with existing laws.

The Ministry of Justice, he further said, is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026 and the Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate.

Gbajabiamila further said: The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.

“The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous and transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for consideration by the President and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly.

“The work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the States Houses of Assembly, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.”

The Presidency had last Thursday hinted that the National Policing Bill will be transmitted to the National Assembly within two weeks.

Gbajabiamila had told newsmen after the steering committee meeting at the State House in Abuja that “The National Policing Bill is more or less ready for transmission to the National Assembly. We will probably have one more meeting after this to cross the t’s and dot the i’s and make sure every area is covered. So, we are 90% ready.

“The governors have one or two observations, and we should be ready in about a week or so.”

He described the bill as ‘the most consequential Bill of the administration so far’ adding that it has undergone strenuous exercises in the last few weeks since the working group’s steering committee began deliberations on August 3, 2026.

Also commenting on the possibility of the states dragging their feet on the passage of the Sixth Constitution Alteration Bill (State Police), especially against the backdrop of the information that only about six states had passed the amendment out of the 36 states and the FCT, Gbajabiamila affirmed that there was a “national consensus” among Nigerians on the need for the amendments.

“I see no reason why anyone will want to have a rethink on it,” he said.

Members of the committee present at the Thursday’s meeting held at the conference hall of the Chief of Staff Office at the State House, Abuja, were Chairman of the Governors’ Forum and Governor of Kwara State, AbdulRazak AbdulRahman; Governors Dapo Abiodun, Ogun State; Uba Sani, Kaduna State; Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, and the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice represented by the Solicitor General and Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Justice, Mrs Beatrice Jedy-Agba.

Others included Chairman, Policy Advisory Committee, Justice Abdullahi Liman (rtd); Head, Nigeria Police Reform Secretariat, Professor Olu Ogunsakin; Special Adviser to the President on National Assembly Matters (House of Representatives), Dr Lanre Smart; Senior Special Assistant to the President on Planning and Research who also doubles as the Secretary of the Committee, Nnadubem Moghalu; representative of the President of the Nigerian Bar Association; and AIG Abraham Nabhon Thomas, representing the National Security Adviser, among others.

President Bola Tinubu had on July 7, 2026, inaugurated the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill to prepare the legal framework for the implementation of state police across the country.

The Working Group’s inauguration followed the National Assembly’s passage of the Constitution Alteration (State Police) Bill, 2026, in which the President proposes a dual policing structure comprising the Federal Police Service and 36 State Police Services.

Tinubu had pisited that while the constitutional amendment creates the framework for state police, the National Policing Bill would provide the legal structure for its implementation.“The Constitution Amendment Bill establishes the framework for dual policing, but it does not operationalise it. That work is left to the National Policing Bill.”

According to him, the proposed legislation would address issues necessary for a smooth operationalisation of the State Police system.

“The proposed National Policing Bill will include provisions on minimum policing standards, state readiness certification, federal-state coordination, accountability, human rights safeguards and fiscal conditions.”

The President said the committee will produce an implementation-ready draft bill immediately after the constitutional amendment process.

“The Working Group has been constituted to produce a technically robust, implementation-ready draft National Policing Bill for transmission to the National Assembly,” Tinubu said.

He said the committee was necessary to avoid delays after the State Police bill passed.

“We must not wait until the constitutional process is concluded before beginning this important assignment,” he said.

World.title: NUJ Honours FCC Commissioner, Peter Eze, for Youth Leadership in Enugu
World.content:
The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Enugu State Council, Correspondents’ Chapel, has honoured the Federal Character Commission (FCC) Commissioner representing Enugu State, Hon. Peter Ogbonna Eze, with an Award of Excellence for Outstanding Youth Leadership.

The award was presented on Thursday night, October 22, 2026, at the grand finale of the 2026 Correspondents’ Chapel Press Week, held at the NUJ Press Centre, Rangers Avenue, Enugu.

Eze was recognised for his contributions to youth empowerment, skills development, talent discovery and efforts to connect young people with employment and career opportunities.

The event was chaired by former Attorney General of Enugu State, Chief Anthony Ani (SAN), and focused on the theme ‘Strengthening Democracy Through Responsible Journalism: 2027 Polls in Focus.’

Other awardees at the event included the Minister of Works, Senator Dave Umahi; Deputy National Chairman South of the APC, Mr Ben Nwoye; the Executive Director of PRODA, Dr Peter Ogbobe, and the Enugu State Commissioner of Police, CP Mamman Bitrus Giwa.

Reacting after receiving the plaque, Eze said he was deeply honoured and humbled because the recognition came from journalists, people whose work is to inform the public, hold leaders accountable and shape opinions.

He thanked the NUJ Correspondents’ Chapel for finding him worthy and asked journalists to continue to stand as the conscience of the nation through courageous reporting, balanced stories and fair judgment.

According to him, the award is not just about what he has done before but a fresh call to do more, adding that he remains committed to creating opportunities for young people and to serving society in a way where leadership is judged not by title but by how many lives it touches.

“The honour is appreciated, the responsibility is understood, and the commitment to service remains unwavering,” Eze said.

Eze’s recognition highlights the importance of youth-focused initiatives amid continuing concerns about unemployment, skills development and economic opportunities for young Nigerians.

A major initiative highlighted was the Peter Eze Youth Connect 2026, which brought together thousands of young people for engagement, mentorship, career guidance and access to professional development opportunities.

The initiative seeks to bridge the gap between young people and available opportunities by connecting them with relevant institutions, professionals and stakeholders who can support their career aspirations and economic advancement.

Through Peter Eze Youth Connect-an event that was adjudged the most popular and impactful youth event in 2026, the FCC commissioner has sought to create platforms for mentorship, career exploration and professional networking, enabling young people to pursue greater economic independence and contribute to societal development.

World.title: Ebola Patient in Nigeria Identified as Wife of Swiss Diplomat
World.content:
Switzerland’s foreign ministry has confirmed that the woman who has tested positive for Ebola in Nigeria is the wife of a Swiss diplomat.

The woman, a 42-year-old Ugandan-born national who lives in the Nigerian capital, Abuja, tested positive for the virus on 20 October, becoming the country’s first confirmed Ebola patient in more than a decade.

They both travelled to Uganda earlier this month. Her husband is currently in isolation but has not developed any symptoms, according to the Swiss foreign ministry.

The ministry told the BBC that all 25 staff at its embassy in Nigeria were in good health and did not need to isolate.

The ministry said the woman had spent about a week at a private clinic in Abuja with symptoms before her diagnosis.

It believes she contracted the virus while travelling in Uganda, although health authorities have yet to establish the source of her infection.

Uganda borders Democratic Republic of Congo, where some 4,600 have died in the country’s most deadly outbreak of Ebola. Two people died in Uganda shortly after the outbreak began in May but it has been declared free of Ebola since August.

The ministry said the decision not to isolate the embassy’s eight Swiss and 17 local employees was taken in consultation with Nigeria’s Ministry of Health and the World Health Organization (WHO).

It added that the embassy remained open and operational, with health and safety measures in place.

The woman is receiving treatment in isolation and is showing signs of improvement, according to the WHO.

She returned to Nigeria on 3 October after spending about two and a half weeks in Uganda.

The patient did ​not travel to DR Congo, the Swiss ‌government told Reuters news agency on Friday, contradicting accounts from Uganda.

She developed symptoms four days after arriving in Abuja and sought treatment at two private health facilities before testing positive for Ebola on 20 October.

Health officials are now investigating whether she may have crossed paths with a Kenyan man who died from Ebola and had travelled through Uganda’s main airport on the same day.

Investigators are examining whether they could have been exposed through shared equipment or other contact, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) said on Thursday.

Dr Wessam Mankoula, the agency’s head of emergency preparedness and response, said this was “one of the possible scenarios”, but stressed that no link had been established.

The Kenyan man had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda before arriving in Nairobi on 3 October. He died shortly afterwards, becoming Kenya’s first recorded Ebola death.

Kenya has since confirmed eight other cases of Ebola.

The WHO said it was too early to determine where the woman in Nigeria became infected.

“The source of exposure is still not known. The travel history of the patient is still being pieced together,” said Dr Patrick Otim, a WHO emergency response official.

He said investigators had struggled to obtain a complete account of her movements because opportunities to interview her were limited while she remained in hospital.

Nigeria’s Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said it was carrying out genomic sequencing, which could help establish whether her infection is linked to other cases. However, it has been confirmed that she has the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, the same one which has caused the outbreak in DR Congo.

“The investigation is reconstructing the full travel and exposure history. Genomic sequencing is given a high priority,” said Dr Pavel Ursu, the WHO’s representative in Nigeria.

Ugandan health officials previously said the woman had travelled to eastern DR Congo for business.

However, the WHO, Africa CDC and Nigeria’s health ministry said they had not received verified information confirming that she had visited the country.

Uganda has maintained that it has no confirmed active Ebola cases and says the woman’s travel through the country does not necessarily mean she contracted the virus there.

Meanwhile, Nigerian authorities are tracing more people who may have been exposed to the woman, beyond the 44 contacts initially identified.

Kenya’s Health Director-General Dr Patrick Amoth said all nine confirmed infections were linked to the first patient, with no evidence of wider community transmission.

He urged the public to remain vigilant and not panic but warned: “We are not out of the woods”.

He said the surviving eight patients were still in isolation and responding well to treatment.

The developments have renewed concerns about the movement of infected people across international borders, particularly between DR Congo and neighbouring Uganda, where thousands cross daily for trade, work and family visits.

Dr Otim warned that the long and porous border between the two countries made it difficult to screen everyone entering or leaving, as many people used unofficial crossing points.

The WHO’s regional director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, called for “regional vigilance” and urged countries to strengthen surveillance, investigate infections and protect frontline health workers.

Ebola is a serious viral disease that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, or with contaminated objects. It does not spread through the air like flu.

The virus can cause fever, severe weakness, vomiting and diarrhoea, and can be fatal. People are not considered infectious before they develop symptoms.

Health authorities say tracing contacts quickly, isolating suspected cases and providing early treatment are crucial to preventing further transmission. (BBC)

World.title: Tech Firm Takes Will Preparation Online to Protect Nigerians’ Assets
World.content:
•Says digital estate planning will expand opportunities for lawyers

Wale Igbintade

A Nigerian technology company, Castle eWill and Trust Limited, has launched a digital estate-planning platform designed to simplify Will preparation, encourage succession planning and make estate-planning services more accessible to Nigerians.

The platform enables adults to prepare, update, securely store and manage their Wills and Trusts online, with the aim of helping individuals protect their families, preserve their assets and ensure that their wishes are respected after death.

The Chief Executive Officer of the company, Mr Olumide Olaiya, said the initiative was founded on the belief that everyone should have the opportunity to plan for the future of their loved ones, regardless of their financial circumstances or location.

According to him, the company hopes to become Africa’s most trusted digital platform for estate planning, Will preparation, Trust administration and probate support.

Olaiya said many Nigerians postponed preparing Wills because they considered the process uncomfortable, complicated or relevant only to wealthy individuals.

He explained that Castle eWill was seeking to change the perception by providing an accessible starting point for estate planning while encouraging users to obtain appropriate professional legal advice.

The platform’s Will preparation process comprises five stages, beginning with the provision of personal information, followed by details of executors, trustees, beneficiaries and assets.

Users are subsequently required to provide particulars of their gifts and wishes, supply information about witnesses, and review and confirm the document before printing it and submitting it to the relevant High Court Probate Registry.

Olaiya said the process was designed to make Will preparation more straightforward while incorporating safeguards to protect users’ information and support the authentication of their documents.

On data protection, the company said files were encrypted before being written to disk, while attempts to access them were logged.

The platform also incorporates identity-verification measures, including email confirmation, authentication of government-issued identification documents and comparison with a live camera check.

According to the company, these measures are intended to establish that the individual making a Will is the person identified in the document.

Another feature is a QR seal attached to every Will generated through the platform.

Castle eWill said scanning the code enables recipients to verify the document’s identity, version and date of issuance, helping institutions, including banks and registries, determine whether a copy is genuine and current.

The platform also sends reminders encouraging subscribers to review their Wills every 12 months and following significant life events that could affect their estate plans.

Such events include marriage, the birth of a child and the acquisition of property.

Addressing concerns that digital Will-making services could diminish the role of legal practitioners, Castle eWill maintained that its platform was intended to expand, rather than undermine, opportunities for lawyers.

The company argued that making estate planning more accessible could bring more Nigerians who had never consulted lawyers about Wills or Trusts into the process, thereby creating additional demand for professional legal services.

The company also expressed its intention to collaborate with lawyers across Nigeria to provide these services.

Drawing a comparison with developments in the banking industry, Castle eWill said the introduction of internet banking and mobile applications had expanded access to banking services rather than eliminated the need for banks and banking professionals.

It maintained that a similar approach could apply to legal services, with technology helping more people take the first step towards succession planning while lawyers provide the expertise required to address complex legal issues.

According to the company, professional legal advice remains particularly important in estates involving complicated family structures, corporate assets, jointly owned properties, customary and Islamic law, foreign assets, taxation, guardianship, business succession and competing claims among beneficiaries.

The company maintained that technology could widen access to estate planning, while professional legal judgment remained essential to ensuring that individuals and families received appropriate advice and that their wishes were properly documented and implemented.

World.title: Knorr Partners CAPA to Celebrate Nigeria’s Culinary Community
World.content:
Knorr has celebrated Nigerian food culture and culinary expertise as the headline sponsor of the Culinary Arts Practitioners Association Nigeria (CAPA) Day 2026. Through its participation, the brand recognised the chefs, caterers and food professionals whose skills and creativity shape the meals that bring people together and make special occasions memorable.

The event was held on Tuesday, at the Hall of Odin, Oniru, Victoria Island, Lagos.

Held under the theme “Root to Relevance,” CAPA Day 2026 explored the relationship between culinary heritage and innovation, with discussions around knowledge sharing, sustainability and the future of food.

Culinary experts, including the president, Chiamaka Nwakalor-Egemba, popularly known as Chef Amaka; the vice-president, Ladipo Ayodeji, known as Chef Dee; and Tolani Tayo-Osikoya, known as Chef T, joined fellow practitioners to celebrate the traditions, skills and ideas shaping Nigeria’s culinary industry.

As part of its participation, Knorr hosted a cooking showcase featuring its Smokey Party Jollof Seasoning, demonstrating how the seasoning could be incorporated into different dishes.

The event also recognised culinary talent through a competition, with Chef Adesuwa Edogun (Chef Eva) emerging in first position, followed by Chef Mujidah Adegbayi (Chef MOA) in second place, Chef Ummulkhuthum (Chef K) in third place, and Chef Adeola Kukoyi in fourth place.

Speaking on Knorr’s sponsorship for this year’s event, Dexter Adeola, Foods Marketing Innovation & EWA Strategy Lead at Unilever, said, “We are proud to be part of CAPA Day 2026 and to support the culinary professionals who play an important role in Nigeria’s food culture. Their skill and creativity help preserve our food traditions while bringing new ideas to the kitchen. Our participation reflects our commitment to celebrating these professionals and the role they play in bringing people together through food.”

The event also marked the induction of new members into CAPA.

World.title: Future Mrs Kolisi? Siya meets Rachel’s parents
World.content:
Siya Kolisi flew to Amsterdam to meet his girlfriend Rachel John's parents. Images via Instagram

Springbok captain Siya Kolisi has flown to Amsterdam to meet his girlfriend, Rachel John’s parents. The rugby player, who is a decade older than his new partner, is set to miss the Stormers’ match against the Scarlets over the weekend.

SIYA KOLISI MEETS THE PARENTS

On his Instagram Stories, Siya Kolisi posted a clip of him mingling with South African artist Vumaala at the Amsterdam Dance Event (ADE), which kicked off on Wednesday, 21 October.

While Siya made no mention of his visit to the country, where his girlfriend Rachel John is originally from, she did.



The curly-haired influencer posted an image of Siya walking beside her father on a trip with her parents.

In the pic, Siya’s back faced the camera, while he appeared deep in conversation with his partner’s dad.

Rachel posted two heart emojis, potentially signifying her love for both her father and Siya.

RACHEL.20?

Siya’s new partner, Rachel John, has left many South Africans questioning if the bubbly brunette could potentially be the future Mrs Kolisi.

Rachel shares the name of Siya’s ex-wife, the mother of his two children.

If the influencer were to marry, could she also become Rachel Kolisi?



Siya’s former spouse has made it clear that she has no plans to legally change her name following her divorce.

Speaking to 947 in March, the former Springbok WAG was asked how she felt about another woman taking on the role of stepmother.

Rachel responded: “I can only parent the best that I can, and that is my priority. Everything else is none of my business”.

World.title: URC Round 4: Lions fall in Edinburgh, Sharks win in Cardiff
World.content:
The Lions stumble against Edinburgh, and the Sharks seal a bonus-point win against Cardiff in the URC Round 4. Image: Lions Rugby website, Sharks Rugby website.

The Sharks and Lions returned to URC action with away clashes on 23 October.

Here are the results from the first two matches of the URC Round 4.

Edinburgh vs Lions

First half (5-3)

The Lions were in action at the Edinburgh Rugby Stadium on Friday night.



Edinburgh went into the clash as the only team still unbeaten in the URC this season, while the Lions were 6th on the table.

Conditions were tricky, with rain falling as the teams ran out onto the pitch.

The Lions tested the hosts early, mauling the ball and floating kicks over the defensive line.



However, Edinburgh easily neutralized the threats and were gifted the ball by the visitors’ frail lineout.

The hosts were the first to score as Matthew Currie finished off a slick team move.

One of the major battles was at the set pieces, with the Lions dominating the scrums.



Chris Smith got the Lions rolling after half an hour, slotting the penalty kick.

Second half (31-10)

It took just two minutes for the hosts to extend their lead through a Mosese Tuipuloto try.



At 51 minutes, Edinburgh created even more distance through a try by Harry Paterson, showing his pace.

The hosts continued to assert their dominance, clearly more comfortable in the damp conditions.

However, the Lions clawed back with a try from Hlekani Batho at close range.



Edinburgh came firing back with 15 minutes left, as Paterson sealed a brace.

Geordie Gwynn was put into space and put the game well and truly to bed.

The hosts remain unbeaten at the top of the table, while the Lions drop to 8th, according to the URC website.



Cardiff Rugby vs Sharks

First half (7-17)

The Sharks continued their away tour with a visit to Cardiff Arms Park on Friday.

Emile van Heerden was honoured by exiting the tunnel first on his 50th appearance for the club.

Andre Esterhuizen became the game’s first casualty when he limped off just 52 seconds in, replaced by Jaco Williams.



The Sharks started perfectly, with Zekhethelo Siyaya offloading for Ethan Hooker to score on his return.

Cardiff withstood the early pressure, running the ball from their half for Josh Adams to cross over.

The Sharks regained the lead through Matt Romao, who ran a good line onto Jordan Hendrikse’s pass.



Cam Winnett was the next player to leave the field after a brutal clash with Edwill van der Merwe at full speed.

The Sharks had the final say of the first half when Jason Jenkins powered his way over.

Second half (21-31)

Cardiff closed the gap to just 3 points after James Botham was muscled over the try line.



Try-scorer Jenkins became another injury concern as he limped off the field, with Stephan Lewies coming on.

At 62 minutes, Cardiff moved ahead from the rolling maul through Botham again.

The Sharks remained in the fight, eventually muscling over through Thomas du Toit.



As momentum swirled, the Durbanites scored from the rolling maul – Ethan Bester was credited with the try.

Romao then scored from the turnover at the death, leaving Cardiff with nothing to show for their efforts.

The Sharks are now up to 2nd on the table, while Cardiff has dropped to 7th.

World.title: Breaking: Mamelodi Sundowns crash out of CAF Champions League while Pirates advance
World.content:
Reigning champions Mamelodi Sundowns have crashed out of the CAF Champions League after drawing 1-1 with Williette on Friday night.

Having played to a goalless draw in Angola, Masandawana needed a victory at Loftus Versfeld to secure their place in the next round. A goalless draw would have forced a penalty shootout, while any scoring draw would see the Brazilians eliminated.

Tashreeq Matthews gave Sundowns an early lead in the 11th minute, raising hopes of progression. However, a defensive mistake allowed the visitors to equalise and put the hosts under pressure.



Sundowns pushed forward in search of a winning goal but failed to find the breakthrough, suffering a disappointing early exit from the continental competition.

Sundowns bow out of CAF

The 1-1 draw on the night left the aggregate score level at 1-1, with Sundowns eliminated on the away-goals rule. It marks the first time since 2015 that the Brazilians have failed to reach the CAF Champions League group stages.

The setback will come as a major blow to Masandawana, who had already won two trophies this season and were hoping to defend their continental crown.

Their rivals Orlando Pirates, meanwhile, secured their place in the group stages after recording an emphatic 5-0 aggregate victory over African Stars on Friday evening.

With their CAF campaign over, Sundowns will now have to turn their attention to domestic competitions, including the Betway Premiership and the remaining cup tournaments, as they look to add to their trophy haul this season.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs fans turn on Mdu Shabalala after costly misses
World.content:
Some Kaizer Chiefs fans have blamed Mduduzi Shabalala following the club’s disappointing early elimination from the CAF Confederation Cup.

Amakhosi were knocked out by Zambian side Red Arrows after losing 3-2 on penalties in the second leg of their second preliminary-round tie in Durban on Friday.

Having suffered a 1-0 defeat in the first leg in Zambia, Chiefs needed a win at home to keep their hopes of progressing to the group stages alive.



They managed to level the aggregate score at 1-1, with Bradley Cross finding the back of the net to force a penalty shootout.

However, Chiefs had opportunities to extend their lead before the match went to penalties, with Shabalala failing to convert two clear chances that could have put the Soweto giants in a stronger position.

Those missed opportunities proved costly as Amakhosi ultimately bowed out of the competition, leaving supporters frustrated with the team’s performance.

Following the disappointing defeat, fans took to social media to voice their frustrations, with some singling out Shabalala for criticism while others questioned the club’s overall direction.

Chiefs fans blame Mdu Shabalala for CAF exit

@Hybreed wrote: “Whoever cursed Kaizer Chiefs, we’re sorry.”

@lucaskagiso added: “Serves us right. I am glad we are out. Don’t want false hopes. Now its up to you KC management to see what you do with this deadwood and clueless technical team.”



@KB_Ramasimong was particularly critical of Shabalala, writing: “Mdu Shabalala …. That guy is a Kwamahlobo type player, he is not improving. How many years has he been missing CLEAR ONE ON ONE chances?….. Even last season he was one of reason we didn’t make KO.”

However, not everyone agreed with the criticism directed at the midfielder, with @MakuaKgothatso highlighting his importance to the team.

“According to most of Kaizer Chiefs fans, when a player miss a clear chance, he is a cow and he does not deserve game time. Without Mdu Shabalala, Chiefs is not functioning,” the supporter wrote.

Chiefs must now turn their attention back to domestic competition after another disappointing result on the continental stage, while the defeat is likely to intensify scrutiny of the team’s performances and the technical team’s decisions.

Whats next for Chiefs?

World.title: Aden McCarthy makes Bafana Bafana preliminary squad
World.content:
Sabah FK defender Aden McCarthy has been named in the Bafana Bafana preliminary squad to face Kenya next month.

Bafana play Kenya in back-to-back Afcon qualifying matches, hoping to secure qualification for next year’s tournament.

On Friday evening, coach Pitso Mosimane named his 38-man preliminary squad for the two matches.



McCarthy, who only had one cap for Bafana, was one of the new names in Mosimane’s squad. This comes after the 22-year-old defender featured in four UEFA Champions League matches.

Speaking to a journalist after scoring against Borussia Dortmund, the former Kaizer Chiefs star paid tribute to fans and his former club.

“The best country in the world. You know, it’s my home, where I come from. I come from a massive team with a massive supporting group, you know. From home, that’s how I always know my people to be. I notice everything. I love my country and the people there. Ja, I appreciate all the support,” McCarthy said.



McCarthy has impressed since leaving Kaizer Chiefs in June, with his performances helping Sabah FK progress through the UEFA Champions League qualifying rounds and into the competition’s main phase.

McCarthy named in Bafana squad

The young defender has continued to attract attention with his displays against some of Europe’s biggest clubs. He previously impressed against Manchester United at Old Trafford before scoring against Borussia Dortmund.

His latest goal further underlined his progress since leaving Naturena, as he continues to represent South Africa on the European stage.



It remains to be seen if Aden McCarthy can make the final Bafana squad.
