Inflation Is Well Below the Target

Consumer prices rose 0.1% in September from August, pushed up by food, fuel and services and held back by cheaper durable goods. Over twelve months inflation reached 1.7%, which is only about half of the bank’s 3.5% target, as the Rio Times reported on 2 October.

Core inflation, which leaves out food and energy prices, was 1.5%. The bank now expects 2026 to end at 3.0%, down from its earlier forecast of 3.3%, and its core forecast fell from 2.8% to 2.2%.

A Stronger Economy Than Expected

Activity in August grew 6.7% from a year earlier, led by electricity, manufacturing and services. The bank then lifted its 2026 growth forecast from 4.5% to 5%, a change the Rio Times covered on 16 October.

Paraguay’s electricity comes mostly from large hydroelectric dams, which is why power output counts for so much in the data. Growth that is strong while inflation is low gives the bank room to wait rather than act.

Oil and US Rates Are the Worry

The committee pointed to Middle East tensions that have kept Brent crude, the world oil benchmark, above US$110 a barrel. Paraguay imports all its fuel, so dearer oil can lift prices at the pump and then ripple through transport and food.

The bank also noted that US inflation rose from 3.4% to 3.7%. Markets now expect the US Federal Reserve to raise rates further, and the dollar gained 1.4% in a month.

What the Guaraní Rate Means in Dollars

At about 5,742 guaraníes (about US$1.00) on 23 October 2026, a loan of 100 million guaraníes is worth about US$17,400. A cheaper dollar would lower the cost of imported fuel, while a stronger one raises it.

Because the Paraguay policy rate stayed at 5.50%, the bank is not using its rate to push the currency either way. It called the stance neutral and pointed to oil and US rates as the risks it is watching.

What It Means for US Readers

US investors in Paraguayan bonds and local companies get a stable backdrop of low inflation and fast growth. A steady Paraguay policy rate means no sudden jump in funding costs for firms that borrow in guaraníes.

US exporters, travellers and lenders should watch the guaraní and oil prices, which the bank names as risks. The decision does not change any tariff, visa or trade rule between the two countries.

What Is Not Known

The central bank has not said whether it expects to cut or raise the Paraguay policy rate at its next meeting. It describes 5.50% as neutral but gives no date for any change.

The size of any oil-driven price rise is also unclear, as is the path of US interest rates through 2027. Neither is something the Paraguayan committee controls.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Paraguay policy rate now?

The Paraguay policy rate is 5.50% a year after the committee’s unanimous vote on Friday 23 October 2026. It was also 5.50% after the July, August and September meetings.

Why did the central bank not cut the rate?

The bank calls 5.50% a neutral setting and worries about oil above US$110 a barrel and higher US interest rates. With inflation expectations at 3.5%, it saw no reason to move.

How high is inflation in Paraguay?

Prices rose 1.7% over the twelve months to September 2026, below the bank’s 3.5% target. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, was 1.5%.

How fast is the Paraguayan economy growing?

Economic activity grew 6.7% in August from a year earlier, and the bank now expects 5% growth for 2026. Its earlier forecast was 4.5%.

How many guaraníes are in a US dollar?

The rate was about 5,742 guaraníes (about US$1.00) on 23 October 2026. That makes 1 million guaraníes worth about US$174.

World.content:

JAMAICA · HURRICANE RECOVERY

Key Facts The country Jamaica is a Caribbean island nation of about 2.8 million people and a major travel destination for Americans.

What happened Of the Jamaica schools hit by Hurricane Melissa, 63 are fully rebuilt and 81 more are 95% to 99% complete.

The storm Melissa struck as a Category 5 hurricane on 28 October 2025 and affected 682 schools.

The spending J$9.2 billion (about US$58 million) has been spent on rehabilitating the damaged schools.

Smaller repairs Repairs are finished at 6 priority-two schools and 1 priority-three school.

Why it matters American travellers, donors and families with ties to the island all have a stake in the recovery.

Jamaica schools hit by Hurricane Melissa are coming back, with 63 of the worst-hit fully rebuilt and 81 more 95% to 99% finished. Officials gave the figures on Thursday 22 October 2026, days before the storm’s first anniversary.

Melissa struck the island as a Category 5 hurricane on 28 October 2025 and affected 682 schools. For US readers, the rebuilding matters for travel, for charities at work there and for families with ties to Jamaica.

Jamaica Schools Rebuilt So Far

Damaged Jamaica schools were sorted into three priority levels, with priority one needing the most extensive work. So far 63 priority-one schools have been fully rebuilt.

Another 81 schools are between 95% and 99% complete, and repairs are finished at 6 priority-two schools and 1 priority-three school. Junior Education Minister Rhoda Moy Crawford gave the figures at the quarterly briefing of the Education Transformation Oversight Committee.

Dr Adrian Stokes, who chairs that committee, said 682 schools were affected by the hurricane in total. The briefing took place at the University of the West Indies regional headquarters on Thursday 22 October 2026.

The recovery follows other storm stories we have covered, including how Jamaica honoured six police officers for Melissa rescue work. The Jamaica Observer reported the school figures on Friday 23 October.

Where the Money Has Gone

Stokes said J$9.2 billion (about US$58 million) has been spent on rehabilitating the damaged schools. At about 158.8 Jamaican dollars to the US dollar on 23 October 2026, the sum is a little under US$58 million.

In June, Education Minister Dana Morris Dixon said the government had secured J$18 billion (about US$113 million) to rebuild hundreds of damaged schools. She spoke at the Jamaica Diaspora Conference in Montego Bay and asked Jamaicans abroad to keep supporting education.

Private donors have helped as well, led by the Sandals Foundation, the charity arm of the Sandals resort group. It reported a J$214 million (about US$1.3 million) restoration of seven schools, with Good 360, a US nonprofit, supplying a library for one of them.

How the New Schools Differ

Officials including Crawford say Jamaica schools are being rebuilt to a higher standard rather than restored to what stood before. The designs follow the Jamaican building code, with extra measures for ceiling height, window design, natural light and cross-ventilation.

Latoya Harris Ghartey of the National Education Trust said roof requirements were raised, and some buildings were converted to slab or steel frames. Builders are also using longer zinc sheets for roofing.

Classrooms get higher ceilings, ceiling fans, better windows and more ventilation to keep them cooler. The new buildings also include wheelchair access for students with disabilities.

What Slowed the Work

Officials named three obstacles: a shortage of skilled labour, difficulty obtaining building materials and problems with contractors. The Jamaica Observer listed these as the main delays.

Morris Dixon said in June that more than 152,000 students and 8,000 teachers were affected. Every school reopened within 90 days, she said, some of them in tents or temporary buildings.

What It Means for US Readers

Jamaica is a short flight from Florida and a favourite destination for American travellers, so the pace of recovery shapes trips and tourism jobs. Schools are also central to family life in communities across the island, so their return matters to relatives abroad.

US groups such as Good 360 and American Friends of Jamaica have already worked on school projects. The government has also asked its diaspora to back literacy, special education, technology and skills training.

The Atlantic hurricane season runs until 30 November, so a new storm remains a risk for unfinished Jamaica schools. The rebuilt schools are designed to withstand future storms, which is the test the programme will face.

What Is Not Known

The Jamaica Observer report gives no completion date for the 81 Jamaica schools that are nearly finished. No student numbers have been given for the 63 rebuilt schools.

The ministry has not broken the J$9.2 billion (about US$58 million) down by school or by funder. Official totals also differ slightly, with 682 schools counted as affected against 681 in the September priority lists.

More: Jamaica news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many Jamaica schools have been rebuilt after Hurricane Melissa?

Officials say 63 priority-one schools have been fully rebuilt. Another 81 schools are between 95% and 99% complete.

How many schools did Hurricane Melissa damage?

Dr Adrian Stokes put the number of affected schools at 682. Melissa struck Jamaica as a Category 5 hurricane on 28 October 2025.

How much has Jamaica spent on school repairs?

Stokes said J$9.2 billion (about US$58 million) has been spent so far. In June the education minister said J$18 billion (about US$113 million) had been secured.

Are Jamaica schools open again?

All Jamaica schools reopened within 90 days of the storm, some in tents or temporary buildings. Permanent rebuilding is still under way at many of them.

Can Americans help rebuild Jamaica schools?

US nonprofits such as Good 360 and American Friends of Jamaica have supported school projects. The education minister has asked the Jamaican diaspora to keep backing education.

World.content:

BRAZIL · UNITED STATES

Key Facts The country Brazil is Latin America’s largest democracy, a country of about 210 million people that votes in a presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

What happened Alexandre Ramagem, convicted of plotting a coup, has been free in Florida since 15 April 2026 while his asylum request is pending.

The sentence Brazil’s Supreme Court sentenced Ramagem to 16 years in prison in September 2025, and he reached the United States on 11 September 2025.

The extradition Brazil’s Ministry of Justice asked Washington to hand him over on 30 December 2025, and no answer has been made public.

The US position The Department of Homeland Security says he overstayed his visa but also that a pending asylum claim gives him no legal status.

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.6% chance of winning the 25 October runoff (23 October, 5:24 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 77% and Kalshi at 76% (Lula: 24% and 25% ), as of 23 October, 5:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

The Brazil spy chief Alexandre Ramagem, sentenced to 16 years, remains free in Florida, CIPER Chile reported on Friday 23 October 2026. The story lands two days before the Brazil election 2026 runoff between President Lula and conservative Flávio Bolsonaro.

For US readers, the case tests whether Washington will send a convicted foreign official home or let an asylum claim keep him in Florida. The latest Brazil election polls call the race close, while Brazil election odds favour Flávio.

Who the Brazil Spy Chief Is

The Brazil spy chief ran Abin, the civilian intelligence agency, under former president Jair Bolsonaro, then served as a deputy for his Liberal Party. Brazil’s Supreme Court sentenced him in September 2025 to 16 years for plotting to overturn the 2022 election.

He left Brazil days later, crossing into Guyana on 9 September 2025 and flying to the United States on 11 September, according to CIPER Chile. Brazil’s Congress stripped him of his seat in December 2025.

How He Stayed Free in the US

Orlando police stopped the Brazil spy chief on 13 April 2026 and handed him to US immigration agents, who said he had overstayed his visa. ICE, the US immigration enforcement agency, released him two days later.

Metrópoles, a Brasília news site, reported that he was freed because he had a pending political asylum request. Homeland Security told CIPER Chile and Agência Pública that such a request gives no legal status, and it has not explained the release.

Brazil’s Extradition Request

Brazil’s Ministry of Justice formally asked the United States to extradite the Brazil spy chief on 30 December 2025. Metrópoles reported in May that Justice Minister Wellington Lima was still waiting for an answer.

Lima said the April detention did not come from the extradition request but from US immigration law. So the request, which Brazil sent through its embassy in Washington, remains open while Ramagem lives in Florida.

The Family Accused of Helping Him

Brazilian federal police files cited by CIPER Chile and Agência Pública, a Brazilian investigative outlet, say the De Mello family housed Ramagem in Florida. Rodrigo de Mello, known as Rodrigo Cataratas, was sentenced in February 2026 to 16 years and 7 months over illegal gold mining on Yanomami land.

Pública reports that Ramagem stayed in the family’s Sole Mia apartment in Miami from 11 September to mid-November 2025. The apartment rents for about R$20,000 (about US$4,000) a month, and Rodrigo denies helping him hide.

What Brazil’s Courts Have Done

Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered Rodrigo’s arrest in December 2025 for helping Ramagem flee. Justice Cármen Lúcia rejected his request for release on 19 October 2026, and the warrant stays open because police cannot find him.

His son Celso, accused of running the mining finances, was arrested in Manaus in December 2025 and wears an ankle monitor, per Agência Pública. His family says he is innocent.

What It Means for US Readers

The Brazil spy chief case shows how US immigration treats a foreign official convicted at home, which matters for ties strained by tariffs. Washington has already called Ramagem an illegal immigrant, so the next step is up to the courts and the State Department.

Investors in Brazilian bonds watch the runoff, because Flávio Bolsonaro has promised a broad amnesty for his father and others convicted in the coup case. A Flávio win could soften Brazil’s push to bring the Brazil spy chief home.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro 76.6% to win the runoff and Lula 23.5% (23 October, 5:24 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has drawn about US$193.2 million in total bets.

These are bets, not polls, and they can move quickly on news. Over the previous 24 hours Flávio’s price slipped by 1.0 point.

What Is Not Known

It is not known when a US judge will rule on the Brazil spy chief’s asylum claim or answer Brazil’s extradition request. DHS has not said why he was released after two days.

The outcome of the runoff may also shape how hard Brazil pushes the case. Neither government has said whether Ramagem could be sent home before a final ruling.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Alexandre Ramagem?

He is the former head of Brazil’s intelligence agency Abin and a former congressman. Brazil’s Supreme Court sentenced him to 16 years in September 2025 for a coup plot.

Why is the Brazil spy chief still free in the US?

He entered the United States on 11 September 2025 and applied for asylum after his visa ran out. A pending claim led to his release by ICE on 15 April 2026, according to Brazilian and Chilean reports.

Has Brazil asked the US to hand him over?

Yes, Brazil’s Ministry of Justice sent a formal extradition request on 30 December 2025. No US answer has been made public.

What does the US government say?

The Department of Homeland Security says Ramagem is in the country illegally because he overstayed his visa. It adds that a pending asylum request confers no legal status and that he will receive due process.

How does this connect to the Brazil runoff?

The runoff on Sunday 25 October pits Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro, who has promised an amnesty for people convicted in the coup case. Ramagem’s fate could depend on who wins.

World.content:

MEXICO · US RELATIONS · SECURITY

Key Facts The country Mexico is the United States’ southern neighbour and top trading partner, led since October 2024 by President Claudia Sheinbaum.

What happened On Friday 23 October 2026 Sheinbaum said Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos told her the former state prosecutor brought CIA agents into a drug-lab raid.

The background Two Americans and two Mexican officers died in a crash after the April raid, and the ex-prosecutor, César Jáuregui, now faces a federal treason case.

The US link President Donald Trump said on Thursday 15 October that operations against the cartels continue and that he has not yet used full force on land.

The next date A federal judge is due to decide on Saturday 24 October whether Jáuregui goes to trial on the treason charge.

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Sheinbaum a 5.0% chance of leaving office by 31 December 2026 (23 October, 5:30 p.m. ET).

Power Index Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 71.4 points (October 2026 edition).

President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Friday 23 October 2026 that Chihuahua’s governor blamed a former state prosecutor for bringing CIA agents into a drug-lab raid. The CIA is the US foreign intelligence agency, and Sheinbaum spoke at her morning press conference in Mexico City.

For US readers it matters because Washington talks of acting against cartels on land, while Mexico prosecutes an official over CIA agents on its soil. The case shows how far Mexico will police any US security work that bypasses the federal government.

What Sheinbaum Said on 23 October

Sheinbaum said Governor Maru Campos told her on Saturday 19 September that former Chihuahua prosecutor César Jáuregui was behind the entry of the CIA agents. When she raised the agents, Campos answered “No fui yo, fue mi exfiscal”, or “It wasn’t me, it was my former prosecutor”, López Doriga reported.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Sheinbaum added that Campos said Jáuregui owned casinos and that this came to light when the prosecutor was moved out of his post. She said she told Campos to file complaints with the competent authorities, replying “Procede”, or “Go ahead”, El Financiero reported.

Sheinbaum also said Federal Attorney General Ernestina Godoy, who leads the FGR prosecutor’s office, was given the same account by Campos. According to Sheinbaum, Godoy was told that the former prosecutor was responsible for the agents’ entry and that corruption had been found.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Two Versions of the CIA Agents Meeting

Campos tells the meeting differently, according to El Financiero. She says it lasted 8 to 10 minutes, that Sheinbaum was defensive, and that the president replied that Campos herself was the one involved.

Sheinbaum said the governor opened the talk at Ciudad Juárez airport by complaining and that both raised their voices. Both women deny any political pact against Jáuregui, which had been widely speculated after his arrest.

The CIA agents dispute matters because Campos belongs to the opposition National Action Party, while Sheinbaum leads the governing Morena party. Jáuregui’s lawyer says the arrest is politically motivated and tied to a quarrel inside the National Action Party in Chihuahua, UnoTV reported on 20 October.

How the CIA Agents Case Reached Federal Court

State and army forces dismantled clandestine drug labs near El Pinal, in Morelos municipality in Chihuahua’s Sierra Tarahumara, between 17 and 19 April 2026. A vehicle returning from the operation fell into a ravine early on Sunday 19 April, and four people died, including two Americans.

Mexican media and officials have described the two Americans as CIA officers, but the CIA has made no public statement on them. Jáuregui resigned on 27 April and was arrested by state officers on Saturday 17 October.

A federal judge ordered him held in pretrial detention on the federal treason charge in the early hours of Wednesday 21 October, Zeta Tijuana reported. The hearing that decides whether he goes to trial is set for Saturday 24 October, after his defence won a longer deadline.

Federal prosecutors say the CIA agents accompanied the state group without federal authorization and that their presence was not reported to superiors. A state judge in Chihuahua separately let one state charge go forward on Thursday 22 October, as described in the court ruling report.

Trump’s Land Warning and Mexico’s Line

On Thursday 15 October Trump told a White House lunch that the cartels control Mexico and that operations against them will continue, Por Esto reported. He said he has not yet launched a full ground attack, as described in the report on his remarks.

Vanguardia columnist Raymundo Riva Palacio argued on 23 October that the April operation already counts as the first US action on the ground. That is his opinion, and no US or Mexican official has announced a US ground offensive.

Sheinbaum has rejected US military operations on Mexican soil as a violation of sovereignty while keeping security cooperation, Por Esto reported. Our earlier report on the leaked names of the two dead officers covers how the identities came out.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket gave Sheinbaum a 5.0% chance of leaving office by 31 December 2026 at 5:30 p.m. ET on Friday 23 October, up 0.4 points. That market has traded about US$292,000 in total, so the price is a thin signal and not a forecast.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

US agencies that work with Mexican state police, including any CIA agents, now face a federal prosecutor who treats unreported cooperation as a possible crime. The federal case rests on Mexico’s National Security Law, which requires foreign agents’ field work to be reported to federal authorities, Vanguardia reported.

Chihuahua, home to many US-owned factories in Ciudad Juárez, sits at the centre of the case. Sheinbaum has said she rejects US military operations on Mexican soil while keeping security cooperation, Por Esto reported.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the federal judge will send Jáuregui to trial on Saturday 24 October. Jáuregui is presumed innocent, and his lawyer argues that nothing shows he knew the Americans would join the raid.

Neither the CIA nor the US government has said publicly who the two Americans worked for or what the CIA agents were doing in Chihuahua. It is also open whether any further US operation on Mexican soil is planned.

More: Mexico news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Sheinbaum say about the CIA agents on 23 October?

She said Governor Maru Campos told her that former prosecutor César Jáuregui was responsible for the agents’ entry into Chihuahua. Campos has given a different account of the same meeting.

Who is César Jáuregui?

He is the former attorney general of Chihuahua, a northern Mexican state that borders Texas and New Mexico. He resigned on 27 April and is held on a federal treason charge that his lawyer calls political.

Have US troops started operations in Mexico?

No US or Mexican official has announced a US military ground operation in Mexico. A Vanguardia columnist argues that the April CIA presence was the first such action, which is his opinion.

Why does this case matter to the United States?

It tests how far Mexico will let CIA agents work with state police without federal approval. It also comes as Trump says operations against the cartels will continue.

What happens next in the case?

A federal judge is due to decide on Saturday 24 October whether Jáuregui is sent to trial for treason. His defence has said it will appeal the separate state ruling of 22 October.

World.title: Brazil Seeks US$38M Under Anti-Faction Law
World.content:
The Justice Palace in Brasília, home of Brazil's Justice Ministry, file photo (Photo: Joehawkins, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ORGANISED CRIME

Key Facts — The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest economy, is home to two violent criminal gangs, the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and the Comando Vermelho (CV).

— Why it matters The state is now going after gang money through civil courts, and Washington has labelled both gangs terrorist groups, which turns their finances into a concern for foreign banks, shippers and exporters.

— Why now The Attorney General’s Office filed the first four lawsuits under the new law on Tuesday 20 October 2026, and the speaker of the Chamber of Deputies welcomed them on Thursday 22 October.

— What happened Brazil asked federal courts in three states to take R$190.3 million (about US$38 million) in assets tied to the PCC and the Comando Vermelho.

— The numbers Four lawsuits, with 87 defendants in three of them, seeking about R$82 million (about US$16.4 million) in three cases and R$108.2 million (about US$21.6 million) in the fourth.

— What it means for you Compliance teams, investors and exporters with Brazilian partners should watch how courts treat the first cases, because they set the pattern for later ones.

— Still open Whether judges approve the seizures, how much is recovered and who the defendants are.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Brazil has used its new Brazil Anti-Faction Law for the first time, asking federal courts to seize R$190.3 million (about US$38 million) in assets tied to the PCC and Comando Vermelho gangs. The Attorney General’s Office, known as the AGU, filed four civil lawsuits on Tuesday 20 October 2026, as O Globo, Valor and Gazeta do Povo reported.

For US readers the filings matter because Washington has labelled the same two gangs terrorist groups, which makes their money a sanctions question for banks, shippers and exporters dealing with Brazil. The AGU says the suits aim at financiers, front companies and relatives, not only at the people directly charged.

Brazil’s Senate has also moved on gang legislation, as we covered in Brazil Senate Panel Votes on Gang Crackdown. Our guide Brazil Security and Crime Explained 2026 gives the background on both gangs.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. How the Brazil Anti-Faction Law Works

Law 15.358 of 2026, known as the Anti-Faction Law, was sanctioned in March 2026 and allows what lawyers call civil forfeiture. It lets the state ask a judge to take assets of illicit origin without waiting for a criminal conviction of the owner.

Gazeta do Povo and iG both reported that this is the first time the AGU has used the law. The AGU’s litigation arm, the Procuradoria-Geral da União, filed the suits in federal courts in the states of Paraná, São Paulo and Rio Grande do Sul.

Forfeiture is not automatic under the Brazil Anti-Faction Law. The AGU has to show a link between the assets and illegal activity, and judges will decide on each request, iG reported.

The AGU said the suits drew on data and studies from the Justice and Finance ministries and the Comptroller General’s Office. The portal iG reported that the Justice Ministry added that tax-authority and court-council data helped identify high-value properties and hidden beneficiaries.

Amounts in reais are converted at the Central Bank of Brazil’s PTAX selling rate of R$5.0140 per US$1 on 20 October 2026. At that rate R$190.3 million is about US$38.0 million.

The Four Lawsuits Filed on 20 October

Three of the suits seek about R$82 million (about US$16.4 million) from 87 defendants in cases linked to the PCC. They stem from Operations Marola, Delivery and Contaminatus, which investigated the smuggling of Paraguayan cigarettes and the sale of banned pesticides.

The fourth suit seeks R$108.2 million (about US$21.6 million) and comes from Operation Hinterland, which investigated cocaine trafficking to Europe and money laundering. The AGU said investigators found financial movements above R$230 million (about US$45.9 million), plus properties, aircraft, luxury cars, companies and gemstones.

The AGU also said investigators found links between people in that case and a Comando Vermelho member, without proof of a formal tie to the gang. Reports therefore describe the four suits as aimed at both gangs, while the AGU stops short of a formal Comando Vermelho link in the Hinterland case.

The AGU said the strategy is meant to reach financiers, economic beneficiaries, front companies and relatives used to hide assets. It added that the tracing work relies on its Asset Recovery Laboratory, known as Labra, and on financial intelligence bodies.

O Globo reported that the cases are proceeding under seal, so it could not verify whether any judge has ruled yet. Valor likewise reported that the suits are under judicial secrecy.

If the courts approve the forfeitures, the money is to go mainly to the National Public Security Fund or to state security funds, Jornal GGN reported. The AGU argued that stripping the gangs of capital could weaken their ability to fund new operations, bribe officials and expand.

Washington Labelled the Same Gangs Terrorists

In late May 2026 the US State Department designated Comando Vermelho and the PCC as Specially Designated Global Terrorists, according to its press release as republished by Small Wars Journal. The Federal Register published the Foreign Terrorist Organization designation of both groups on Friday 5 June 2026.

As we reported in US Warns Americans Over Ties to Brazil PCC and Comando Vermelho, US officials later said that dealing with the gangs can carry risk for Americans as well. The Brazilian forfeiture suits are a separate domestic legal track and do not themselves apply US sanctions.

Hugo Motta, speaker of Brazil’s Chamber of Deputies, welcomed the filings on Thursday 22 October in a social media post, writing that this is how you fight a gang, by taking its money. The Chamber’s news agency noted that Motta recalled the bill won 370 votes in the lower house.

What It Means for You

For investors and companies with Brazilian exposure, the filings show the state targeting assets linked to cross-border trade, farm chemicals, aviation and property. The cases described so far involve cigarette smuggling, pesticides and cocaine, and the reports reviewed name no listed company.

Compliance teams that handle Brazilian counterparties will want to follow how the courts treat these first cases, because they set the pattern for later ones. Our guides Brazil Power Structure Explained 2026 and Brazil Freezes About US$99 Million in Nationwide Organised Crime Raids show how earlier asset freezes unfolded.

Travellers and residents in the country’s largest city can find local context in our São Paulo expat city guide. One of the four suits was filed in São Paulo, though the reports reviewed do not say which assets are located there.

What Is Not Known

The AGU’s own announcement was not opened for this article, so the details rest on O Globo, Valor, Gazeta do Povo, Jornal GGN and iG, which agree on the amounts, the courts and the law number. Court decisions, the names of the defendants and the exact assets listed are not public because the cases are under seal.

It is not known when judges will rule, how much will ultimately be recovered, or whether the legal basis will face a constitutional challenge. The reports reviewed give no estimate of how much money the gangs hold in total.

Whether and how US authorities will use the Brazilian filings is also unknown. Nothing in the reports reviewed says Washington has commented on them.

Background: Brazil Election Polls: Flávio 51%, Lula 49%.

Background: Brazil Tax Reform 2026 Replaces Five Taxes With Two VATs.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Brazil’s Anti-Faction Law?

Law 15.358 of 2026 was sanctioned in March 2026 and lets the state seek forfeiture of illicit assets without a prior criminal conviction. Judges must still approve each request.

How much is Brazil trying to seize?

The AGU is seeking R$190.3 million (about US$38 million) in four civil lawsuits filed on 20 October 2026. Three suits seek about R$82 million (about US$16.4 million) and one seeks R$108.2 million (about US$21.6 million).

Which gangs are targeted?

The suits target assets tied to the PCC and the Comando Vermelho. In the Hinterland case the AGU found a link to a Comando Vermelho member but no proof of a formal tie to the gang.

Has the United States designated these gangs?

The State Department designated both as Specially Designated Global Terrorists in late May 2026, and the Federal Register published their Foreign Terrorist Organization designation on 5 June 2026. The Brazilian forfeiture suits are separate from that US action.

Have courts ruled on the seizures?

Not as far as is public, because the cases are under seal. O Globo said it could not verify whether any decision has been made.

World.title: Canada Denies US Claim of Midterm Meddling
World.content:
CANADA · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening The US Embassy in Ottawa said on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, that Canadian officials are trying to influence the November 3 US midterm elections.

— Why it matters The charge lands in the middle of a tariff fight between two countries that are each other’s largest trading partners.

— The numbers The embassy lists 11 Canadians charged or sentenced for illegal US voting between 2012 and 2024, in elections from 2012 to 2024.

— Who is who Prime Minister Mark Carney, Industry Minister Mélanie Joly and Ontario Premier Doug Ford reject the claim.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Democrats 91.5% to win the US House and 67.5% to win the Senate (23 October 2026, 5:18 pm ET).

Canada says it is not meddling in the US midterm elections, after the US Embassy in Ottawa accused Canadian politicians of trying to sway them. The row matters to American readers because it could make tariff talks with their largest trading partner more political before voters go to the polls on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

The embassy published a fact sheet on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, saying the Canadian government is dismissing concerns about potential interference in US elections. Ottawa has denied it, and the reporting we reviewed shows no finding that any law was broken.

This analysis explains what is alleged, what the public record shows and what it could mean for US-Canada trade. It builds on our USA and Canada Intelligence Brief and our guide to Canada’s counter-tariffs.

What the US Embassy Says Canada Did

The fact sheet, titled “Monitoring Canadian Activities in U.S. Politics,” names four Canadian figures. It ends with the line “Americans decide America’s elections.”

Industry Minister Mélanie Joly met Democratic officials, including in Boston, in September. Asked about it, she said that was “exactly why I’m meeting so many governors and potential presidential candidates.”

Ontario Premier Doug Ford wrote to Prime Minister Carney in August proposing retaliatory tariffs on states that are politically significant to the current US administration’s base. Ontario also ran an anti-tariff advertising campaign that used Ronald Reagan clips, launched in early 2025.

Liberal MP Anthony Housefather campaigned in Florida for Democratic Representative Debbie Wasserman Schultz before her August primary. The fact sheet also points to an October 13 roundtable in Vermont on tariffs, attended by Bernadette Jordan, Canada’s consul general in Boston, and Democratic Representatives Becca Balint and Jim McGovern.

US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra had sounded the alarm a week earlier. In a podcast interview on October 14 he said, “We are monitoring it,” and that “if some of it becomes election interference, America will respond.”

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

In Plain English: Who Is Involved

The embassy is the US government’s office in Ottawa, led by Ambassador Pete Hoekstra. Global Affairs Canada is Canada’s foreign ministry, which runs its embassies and consulates abroad.

Mélanie Joly is Canada’s industry minister, and Doug Ford runs Ontario, Canada’s most populous province. Housefather is a member of Parliament from the governing Liberal Party.

Canada’s Answer and the Evidence So Far

Prime Minister Carney said on October 16 that “we don’t get ourselves involved in their elections, they don’t get themselves involved in our elections.” After the fact sheet appeared he said that “all of our actions are in the interest of Canadian workers, Canadian families and the future of this economy.”

Joly rejected the charge on October 15, saying her meetings aim to attract investment to Canada. Ford said Ontario will “focus on what we can do here in Ontario.”

The fact sheet rests on public statements, meetings, an advertising campaign and a campaign appearance. The reporting we reviewed describes no finding of covert activity or unlawful interference.

The one criminal-law item is a list of 11 Canadians charged or sentenced for illegal voting between 2012 and 2024. The fact sheet does not tie those cases to the Canadian government.

Canadian Diplomats Told to Keep Their Distance

CBC reported that Global Affairs Canada sent two notices in the past month to its US missions. Staff were told to avoid appearing with midterm candidates, to refrain from taking sides on social media and to avoid photos with candidates.

The ministry called the advice routine. It said “Government officials are always instructed to limit public events and stakeholder engagement during election periods in their host country.”

Trucks queue at the Blue Water Bridge crossing at Port Huron, Michigan. File photo.

Why Tariffs Sit Behind the Dispute

The embassy’s examples all circle one subject: Canada’s response to US tariffs. Ottawa says it is defending Canadian workers, while Washington says some of the same moves look like pressure on American voters.

Lobbying governors, lawmakers and businesses is normal trade diplomacy. The line becomes contested when officials link tariff outcomes to which party wins.

For companies with cross-border supply chains, the risk is slower talks rather than a sudden break. Fewer public meetings between Canadian officials and US politicians could mean less visible progress before November 3.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a real-money prediction market, priced a Democratic win in the US House at 91.5% and in the Senate at 67.5% on 23 October 2026 at 5:18 pm ET. Traders had wagered about US$21.1 million on the House market and US$8.8 million on the Senate market.

These prices cover the midterm result, not the interference claim, and no active market on that claim was found. Prices are bets, not polls.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

If you invest in or run a business with exposure to US-Canada trade, expect more guarded public messaging from Ottawa until the vote. The dispute does not signal a breakdown in relations.

For readers elsewhere, the case shows how trade lobbying can be recast as election politics. Other governments that press Washington on tariffs may watch how this plays out.

What Is Not Known

The embassy has not said what, if anything, it will do next. No public evidence shows that Carney or his office directed any effort to influence US voters.

It is also unclear how long Canada’s diplomatic guidance will stay in force. The reporting we reviewed gives no end date.

What to Watch

Watch for any further embassy statements before Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and for whether candidates take up the issue in the final days. After the vote, the question is whether tariff talks resume with less political heat.

Frequently Asked Questions

What exactly did the US Embassy allege about Canada?

On October 21, 2026, the embassy said Canadian officials were trying to influence the November 3 midterms. It cited Joly’s meetings, Ford’s tariff proposal, Housefather’s campaigning, a consul general’s event and an Ontario ad campaign.

How did Canada respond to the claim?

Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada does not involve itself in other countries’ elections. Industry Minister Mélanie Joly said her meetings aim to attract investment, and Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Ontario will focus on protecting its economy.

Is there evidence of election interference?

The reporting we reviewed describes no finding of unlawful interference. The fact sheet relies on public statements, meetings, an ad campaign and a campaign appearance.

What did Global Affairs Canada tell its diplomats?

Staff in the United States were told to avoid appearing with midterm candidates, avoid taking sides on social media and avoid photos with candidates. The ministry called this routine guidance for election periods.

When are the US midterm elections?

Tuesday, November 3, 2026. All of the US House and about a third of the Senate are on the ballot.

How could this affect US-Canada trade talks?

It may make public engagement more cautious and talks more political before the vote. It does not by itself change either side’s tariff positions.

World.title: Lula Says Court Has His Card, Flight Data
World.content:
The headquarters of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) in Brasília, where a judge is weighing the Lula campaign complaint against Meta. File photo, December 2025. (Photo: O Tribunal da Democracia, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Friday, 23 October, 5:25 p.m. ET · Source: Poder360, Metrópoles, CNN Brasil

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. What happened Lula’s campaign says it gave the electoral court (TSE) its corporate-card records, flight records and a waiver for bank, tax and phone data. The dispute Flávio Bolsonaro’s side disputes what was actually delivered, and each camp wants more from the other. Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition). Prediction markets Kalshi traders put a Flávio win by at least 1 point at 76% and a Lula win by at least 1 point at 16% (23 October, 5:21 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 76% and Kalshi at 75% (Lula: 24% and 25% ), as of 23 October, 5:20 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls. Still open Whether the court will collect both candidates’ records and publish them together before the vote.

Lula’s presidential campaign said on Friday 23 October that it has handed Brazil’s electoral court (TSE) records of the government corporate card, the president’s agenda and Air Force (FAB) flights, Poder360 reported. The papers were filed on Thursday night, according to CNN Brasil and Metrópoles, two days before the runoff.

The campaign also signed waivers that let the court look at bank, tax and phone records of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, and his family. The Brazil election 2026 pits Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro, the conservative senator for Rio de Janeiro.

What Lula’s Campaign Says It Delivered

Poder360 lists the corporate card of the Presidency, the agenda of first lady Janja Lula da Silva, the president’s own commitments and FAB flight records. CNN Brasil says the campaign handed over “all data to which it has access.”

Metrópoles reports that the campaign also asked the TSE to act as a neutral referee. It wants “integral, simultaneous and reliable disclosure” of both candidates’ data, it said.

Edinho Silva, president of Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT), said data offered without arbitration or validation weakens its credibility with society, Metrópoles reported. The court had not published the documents when those reports appeared.

The plenary chamber of Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) in Brasília. File photo. Photo: Alejandro Zambrana/Secom/TSE, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

How the Records Fight Began

Lula challenged his rival during the Band television debate on Sunday 18 October, and Flávio accepted. Flávio then added conditions, including the card spending, Janja’s agenda and the secrecy of Lula’s former chief of staff, Metrópoles reported.

Justice André Mendonça of the TSE ruled that candidates may publish their own data without a judge. Lula’s side asked him to reverse that, and our earlier report on the request to reconsider has the detail.

CNN Brasil says Flávio’s campaign filed only authorizations and disputes what Lula’s side actually delivered. It adds that Mendonça would have to request the data from the central bank, banks, the tax authority and phone firms, with no timeline given.

What It Means for US Readers

Brazil is Latin America’s largest economy, and its next president will set its stance on trade and investment. Court fights in the final days can move Brazilian shares, bonds and the real, including US-listed Brazilian stocks.

The dispute does not change the vote itself. It decides whether voters see both candidates’ records before Sunday.

Our Brazil election polls tracker lists every survey.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Kalshi, a prediction market regulated in the US by the CFTC, traders price a Flávio Bolsonaro win by at least 1 point at 76% and a Lula win by at least 1 point at 16% (23 October, 5:21 p.m. ET). The margin contracts have traded about 35,000 and 45,000 contracts.

These are bets, not polls, and they can move fast on new surveys. Our Brazil election odds page tracks Polymarket and Kalshi.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether Mendonça will order the data collected, or whether the full TSE bench will step in before Sunday. We could not verify the documents themselves, which the court has not released.

The filing was made on Thursday night, while the campaign’s public statement came on Friday. This report covers the legal dispute only, not any claim about either candidate’s finances.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Lula’s campaign give the electoral court?

It says it delivered corporate-card records, the first lady’s agenda, flight records and waivers for bank, tax and phone data. The court has not published them.

Why is Flávio Bolsonaro’s side unhappy?

It disputes what Lula’s campaign actually delivered, CNN Brasil reports. It filed only authorizations of its own and set conditions for opening its records.

Will voters see the records before the runoff?

That is not clear. The court would first have to request the data from banks, the tax authority and phone firms.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October. The runoff is between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

World.title: Court Bars Ban on Lula’s WhatsApp Channel
World.content:
A Federal Justice building that houses federal special courts in Goiânia, one of the cities served by the First Regional Federal Court. File photo, 2023. (Photo: Emerson Júnior GSF, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Friday, 23 October, 2:20 p.m. ET · Source: Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) statement, as reported by CNN Brasil and Jovem Pan

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, holds its presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened On Friday 23 October, Brazil’s electoral court said it has not ordered any WhatsApp channel taken offline.

Why it matters Both campaigns are fighting in court over a pro-Lula channel with more than 9 million followers, two days before the vote.

The rule A draft would have suspended political channels with over 200,000 followers from 48 hours before to 24 hours after voting.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.1% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 23.5% (2:16 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 77% and Kalshi at 76% (Lula: 23% and 24% ), as of 23 October, 6:00 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open Meta’s technical report on the channel and the ruling on the Lula campaign’s court challenge had not been published when we checked.

Brazil’s electoral court said on Friday 23 October that it has not ordered any WhatsApp channel off the air, after a week of fights over a pro-Lula channel. The statement came two days before the Brazil election 2026 runoff, as reported by CNN Brasil and Jovem Pan.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 50.9 %, Lula 49.1 % 40 national polls from 20 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

The court, formally the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), runs Brazil’s elections and judges campaign disputes. Rumours of an imminent ban on the “Exército do Lula” (Lula’s Army) channel had spread among supporters, and the court answered them directly.

What the Electoral Court Said

The TSE said in a note that it “did not order the removal of any WhatsApp channel,” according to CNN Brasil and Jovem Pan. It called inferences drawn from its short-deadline requests for information “absolutely improper.”

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Those requests refer to the order of Thursday 22 October, when court president Kassio Nunes Marques gave Meta, the owner of WhatsApp, 24 hours to deliver a technical report on the channel. Our report on that order has the details.

Platforms Asked to Act Evenly

Nunes Marques met representatives of Meta, X, Google, TikTok and Kwai, a short-video app, according to CNN Brasil. He asked them for more staff and for “even-handed” action toward the two candidates during the runoff, the outlet reported.

The aim is to keep both camps under the same rules for the final days. The court gave no deadline beyond the runoff weekend in the reports we reviewed.

The Draft Ban That Sparked Alarm

Court vice-president André Mendonça drafted a proposal to suspend political channels with more than 200,000 followers from 48 hours before to 24 hours after voting, Jovem Pan reported. It would have hit channels backing both Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, which is why the proposal drew attention.

We covered it when it emerged: Court Weighs Ban on Big WhatsApp Channels.

Nunes Marques told Folha de S.Paulo he opposed “changes to electoral resolutions on the eve of elections,” according to Folha reports cited by Jovem Pan. He distanced himself from the draft.

The Lula Campaign Goes to Court

Lula’s campaign filed a writ of security, an urgent court challenge, against Nunes Marques’s decisions on the channel, Folha de S.Paulo and Poder360 reported. It argues that the court presidency has no power to block a user-run channel by administrative order and that suspending it on a fear of future violations amounts to prior censorship.

The channel is run by federal deputy André Janones and has more than 9 million followers, according to CNN Brasil. Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign had asked the court to suspend it, and it has been suspended and restored several times since 11 October.

What It Means for You

For investors in Brazilian assets, an unsettled fight over campaign rules adds noise to a race already moving prices. Our Brazil election odds page tracks how traders are pricing it.

For US readers following online political speech, the case tests how far an election court may restrict private messaging channels. The court’s denial lowers the near-term risk of a sweeping shutdown, but the pending challenge keeps the dispute open.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.1% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 23.5% (2:16 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has drawn about US$192.8 million in total bets.

World.title: Costa Rica Could Lose 24-Hour Tsunami Monitoring Over University Cuts
World.content:
Costa Rica’s tsunami warning center says it will stop round-the-clock monitoring of the country’s coasts on Jan. 1, 2027, unless the government and lawmakers restore funding cut from public universities in next year’s budget. The National Tsunami Monitoring System (Sinamot), run by the National University (UNA), has served as Costa Rica’s tsunami alert center since April 2014.

It is the team that assesses, within minutes of a major earthquake in the Pacific or the Caribbean, whether waves headed for Costa Rica pose a danger. In a statement released yesterday, Sinamot said a staff position funded every year since 2018 will not be financed in 2027. Coordinator Silvia Chacón said the program, which currently has three or four staff members, would be left with two people, one working three-quarters time and the other half time.

Chacón said that would make it impossible to fulfill the center’s main purpose of alerting the country when a tsunami could strike its coasts. With that staffing, several hours of each day would go unmonitored, and the center says it would have to suspend real-time threat analysis. The university links the cut to the government’s proposal for no increase in the Special Fund for Higher Education (FEES) in 2027, and to further reductions in the Legislative Assembly. UNA Rector Jorge Herrera told Sinamot that the staff reduction followed both decisions, according to the center.

The Assembly’s budget committee approved a motion shifting ₡8,048 million (about $17.6 million) from the five public universities to the Ministry of Public Education to cover employer obligations to the teachers’ pension fund. The measure must still clear the full legislative process.

Much of Sinamot’s work never makes headlines because it consists of ruling threats out. In 12 years, the center has evaluated more than 900 events with tsunami potential. Eight produced tsunamis recorded in Costa Rica, three required preventive measures such as suspending water activities, and five were seen by people on the coast.

Sinamot official Kristel Espinoza described one case in which the U.S.-based Pacific Tsunami Warning Center warned that waves of 1 to 3 meters (3 to 10 feet) could reach Costa Rica. She said the national team analyzed the data within 15 minutes and determined that no evacuation was needed.

International centers issue general warnings for entire ocean regions, and those warnings require local evaluation to determine what they mean for a specific coastline. Recent events handled by the center include the Tonga volcanic eruption in January 2022 and the earthquake off Kamchatka, Russia, in July 2025.

The center has also worked with more than 70 coastal communities, produced tsunami hazard studies for both coasts and carried out site-specific analyses for Cahuita, Carrillo, Sámara, Tamarindo and Bahía Potrero. It runs three to five tsunami drills a year. Sinamot has asked the government and the Legislative Assembly to adopt measures that would keep the tsunami alert service running through 2027, and says a solution guaranteeing the staff it needs must be in place before January.

No public response from the Ministry of Finance or the National Emergency Commission had been reported as of yet. The warning adds to concerns raised by other university-run public services, including the national road-quality laboratory LanammeUCR, which has said a ₡250 million (about $550,000) cut will affect its oversight work.

World.title: Costa Rica Declares Its First Red Alert at Sea as El Niño Drought Hits Guanacaste
World.content:
If you live in Guanacaste or on the southern tip of the Nicoya Peninsula, or you’re heading there soon, you’re now in the part of Costa Rica the government considers hardest hit by El Niño. The National Emergency Commission (CNE) raised 10 areas and three Puntarenas districts to red alert for drought yesterday.

For the first time, the red alert also covers the sea. A strip about 22 kilometers (12 nautical miles) wide along the entire Pacific coast is now included, because warmer water is hurting the small and mid-sized fishing operations that depend on it. The red alert covers Abangares, Bagaces, Cañas, Carrillo, Hojancha, La Cruz, Liberia, Nandayure, Nicoya and Santa Cruz, plus the districts of Paquera, Cóbano and Lepanto. That takes in beach towns such as Tamarindo, Playas del Coco, Nosara, Santa Teresa and Montezuma.

Thirteen more areas are on orange alert: Tilarán, Puntarenas, Esparza, Montes de Oro, Monteverde, Orotina, San Mateo, Garabito, Parrita, Quepos, Dota, Tarrazú and León Cortés. Another 48 are on yellow, including San José, Escazú, Desamparados, Alajuela, Heredia, Cartago, Pérez Zeledón, Osa and Golfito.

In all, 71 areas now carry some level of El Niño alert, with yellow signaling the need to prepare, orange requiring public agencies to mobilize personnel and resources, and red indicating an active emergency response. The reason being is that the rain hasn’t come, with the North Pacific receiving 43% less rainfall than normal from January through September, according to the National Meteorological Institute (IMN), while Cañas recorded an even greater shortfall of 63%.

The Central Pacific came in 37% below normal, the South Pacific 27% and the Central Valley 20%. That gap matters more than usual because October is normally one of the wettest months of the year, when rivers, reservoirs and aquifers fill up before the dry season. A dry October means Costa Rica heads into summer with less water stored.

If you’ve seen heavy downpours and flooding lately, you’re not imagining it. The CNE said recent storms in some areas don’t cancel out the deficit elsewhere. The North Caribbean has had 39% more rain than normal and parts of Limón more than 70% more, while the Pacific keeps drying out.

The ocean is part of the problem as the pacific waters off Costa Rica have run about 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warmer than normal, and the CNE says sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific over the past five months are the highest recorded since 1950.

A key El Niño indicator has reached 2.2 degrees Celsius (4 degrees Fahrenheit) above normal, which puts the event in the “very strong” category. The IMN expects that intensity to hold from November through January, just as the dry season sets in, and has said El Niño’s effects could last well into 2027.

CNE President Alejandro Picado said the aim is to get ahead of the impacts, protect the population and keep essential services running. Public institutions have carried out more than 200 measures since May covering water supply, energy, food production, commerce and vulnerable communities.

What you can do now to help the situation is fix leaks, don’t waste water and go easy on electricity, Picado said. Costa Rica gets most of its power from hydroelectric dams, so a drought squeezes the grid as well as the taps, and every liter saved now is still in the system at the end of the dry season, when rivers run lowest.

The alerts will stay in place over the coming months while authorities track how the event develops. We’ll keep you posted.

World.title: No Roads, No Cars, Just Tarpon at Costa Rica’s Silver King Lodge
World.content:
Long before Costa Rica became known for surf towns and zip lines, the remote corner where the Río Colorado spills into the Caribbean was known to a small circle of anglers as the finest tarpon water on the planet. Barra del Colorado still sits at the edge of the map, reachable only by boat or small plane.

It remains something of a secret even at home, and many Costa Ricans have never been. Under new ownership, Silver King Lodge is giving travelers a reason to make the trip. The Río Colorado branches off the San Juan River near the Nicaraguan border and winds through lowland rainforest to the sea. Most of its course runs through the Barra del Colorado National Wildlife Refuge, about 81,177 hectares (200,600 acres) of rivers, wetlands and forest.

The village is a scatter of wooden houses raised on stilts along the riverbanks, a short airstrip and a handful of lodges. There are no roads in and no cars in town. The river is the highway, and the day runs on boats, tides and rain. Schoolchildren ride a boat to class each morning, every one of them in a life jacket. It is a small community that looks after its own, and that warmth extends to the visitors who make the long trip.

The modern story of Barra begins with Casa Mar. In the late 1960s, Carlos Barrantes, a San José tackle shop owner, found the river full of tarpon that no one had ever fished with a fly. With backing from a U.S. financier, he built a lodge on Laguna Agua Dulce, a short boat ride from the sea and the Nicaraguan border.

Casa Mar’s longtime owner and manager was Bill Barnes, a former physical education teacher from South Florida who took over in the early 1970s. Under Barnes, the lodge became the place where much of modern tarpon fly fishing was worked out. In the 1970s, anglers at Casa Mar fishing lead-core shooting heads developed many of the deepwater fly techniques now used around the world. Harry Kime spent about three months a year there for several seasons, fishing tarpon almost every day. Dan Blanton, Del Brown and Lefty Kreh were among the regulars.

“All the top American flyfishermen came to Casa Mar,” Casa Mar veteran Peter Gorinsky told writer Dave Sherwood, whose history of the lodge appeared in The Flyfish Journal. Kreh, a good friend of Barnes, later said more tarpon had likely been caught at Casa Mar than anywhere else on Earth, according to Sherwood’s account.

Success brought competition. Isla de Pesca, Tarponland, Silver King and the Río Colorado Lodge founded by Archie Fields all opened along the river and its lagoons. For a time the boom brought jobs to the village and an improved airstrip. Harder years followed. In the 1980s, Nicaragua’s civil war played out just across the border and kept many visitors away. Barnes died in 2002, and his ashes were scattered on the Río Colorado and at Casa Mar.

Afterwards, the lodge never regained its footing and in the years that followed, the jungle reclaimed much of the old lodge. Silver King, which opened on the banks of the Río Colorado in the early 1990s, outlasted most of its neighbors. The lodge stands on pilings above the river’s flood line. Covered wooden walkways link the rooms, dining hall and common areas, so guests stay dry even in a tropical downpour.

It takes up to 24 guests at a time, which keeps the atmosphere close. The lodge changed hands in 2025 and its new owner has fished Barra for 30 years and set out to restore the relaxed, welcoming character that made the place special. Fishing is still the heart of it. Guides work the river mouth for giant tarpon and the backwaters for lighter-tackle species. The on-site tackle shop is stocked well enough that guests don’t need to bring their own rods.

The lodge has the only IGFA-certified scale in Barra, which matters to anglers chasing world records. Snook, tripletail and several other species offer real record opportunities on this water. The captains are local men who grew up on this river, many from families that have guided here for decades. They are bilingual, patient with beginners, sharp with experienced fly casters and always ready with a story about the fish that got away.

Meals are served buffet style, with fresh local seafood and Costa Rican dishes alongside American and European favorites, plus a different homemade dessert each day. Dinners run long and loud, and the open bar keeps the stories going well after dark. Howler monkeys announce the dawn, and the gardens and river edges draw a steady parade of wildlife.

Birders who download Merlin, the free identification app from the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, can spend an afternoon logging Caribbean lowland species rarely seen on the Pacific side. Others claim a hammock, the pool or the sauna and let the river do the rest. Most guests take a 25-minute flight from San José that lands on the village airstrip, and the transfer is included in the lodge’s packages. Others travel overland to the Caribbean side and finish the trip by boat through the canals.

Rooms measure more than 41 square meters (450 square feet), with 3.7-meter (12-foot) wild cane ceilings, hardwood walls and air conditioning. Free Starlink Wi-Fi keeps guests connected. Reservations can be made through Silver King Lodge at 1-800-610-1333 or 352-422-5214, or by email at william@silverkinglodge.com.

Casa Mar’s heyday is long past, but its spirit lives on along the Colorado. The river still runs to the sea, the guides still know every bend and the howlers still call from the canopy. At Silver King, the old Barra is very much alive.

World.title: Francisco Cerundolo Reaches Brussels Quarterfinals With Win Over Martin Damm
World.content:
Argentina’s Francisco Cerundolo advanced to the European Open quarterfinals yesterday, beating American Martin Damm 6-4, 7-6 (4) to set up a meeting with French qualifier Clement Chidekh. The third-seeded Argentine closed out the second set in a tiebreak to reach the last eight at the ATP 250 tournament. His victory gave Argentina a quarterfinalist on a day when compatriot Mariano Navone was eliminated.

Cerundolo’s serve helped him through the match. He hit 12 aces and saved six of the seven break points he faced, limiting Damm’s opportunities to turn pressure into a lead. The American finished with 36 unforced errors, compared with Cerundolo’s 20. Damm, who entered the main draw as a lucky loser after losing in qualifying, pushed the second set to a tiebreak. Cerundolo took it 7-4 to finish the match without needing a deciding set.

The 28-year-old now faces an opponent enjoying a breakthrough week. Chidekh beat Britain’s Jacob Fearnley 7-6 (4), 6-2 to reach his first ATP Tour quarterfinal, following an earlier victory over seventh seed Botic van de Zandschulp. Cerundolo entered the week ranked No. 21, while Chidekh was No. 152. The Frenchman’s results in Brussels, however, have already carried him past two main-draw opponents after coming through qualifying.

Navone could not join Cerundolo in the quarterfinals. The eighth-seeded Argentine lost 7-6 (4), 7-5 to Tallon Griekspoor of the Netherlands, with both sets decided by narrow margins. The European Open continues through October 25. For Cerundolo, the next step is a match against Chidekh for a place in the semifinals.

World.title: Gian Teck begs court for mercy after pleading guilty to having sex with 14-year-old girl; ‘Didn’t know what he was doing’ despite previous case involving other 14-year-old girl
World.content:
Gian Teck begs court for mercy after pleading guilty to having sex with 14-year-old girl; ‘Didn’t know what he was doing’ despite previous case involving other 14-year-old girl

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Twenty-two-year-old Gian Teck, who pleaded guilty to unlawful sexual intercourse with a 14-year-old girl, appeared before Justice Nigel Pilgrim in the High Court on Thursday, October 22, where he pleaded for forgiveness and mercy ahead of his sentencing. Notably, this is Teck’s second offense for sex with a 14-year-old girl involving a minor in a separate incident.

“I just want to ask for forgiveness from the court. I didn’t know what I was doing at the moment. I want the court to consider me and have mercy on me,” Teck said during his mitigation hearing.

Teck was 18 years old when he engaged in sexual intercourse with the minor at his home on June 5, 2023. He initially denied the charge but changed his plea to guilty on October 1, on the fourth day of his trial, after the victim testified behind closed doors.

His attorney, Javier Williams, urged the court to impose a sentence at the lower end of the sentencing range, arguing that Teck was young and immature at the time of the offense and had no previous convictions.

Crown Counsel Kirk Brown, representing the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, argued that Teck should receive only a limited reduction in his sentence because his guilty plea came after the trial had already begun and the victim had been required to testify.

While both sides discussed a sentencing range of two to four years under the applicable sentencing guidelines, Brown maintained that the court should not impose a sentence below the five-year statutory minimum. The offense carries a prison term of five to ten years.

The prosecution also raised concerns about the possibility of Teck reoffending and requested that the court order counselling as part of his rehabilitation.

According to the agreed facts, the minor visited Teck’s home on June 5, 2023, where they engaged in sexual intercourse. During a subsequent police interview, Teck admitted having sexual intercourse with the girl on three occasions but claimed he believed she was 15 years old.

Teck had previously faced separate allegations involving another 14-year-old girl. However, that case was discontinued in January 2026 after the complainant declined to testify. Justice Candace Nanton explained at the time that the prosecution’s decision to enter a nolle prosequi did not amount to an acquittal and that the charges could be brought again.

Justice Pilgrim reserved his sentencing decision to consider the submissions made by both sides. Teck is scheduled to learn his fate on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.
